# APA-style table formatting (no vertical rules, horizontal rules only,
# serif font) so tables can be copy-pasted straight into a manuscript.
# Replaces kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "hover", ...) everywhere.
# One p-value style for every report table: no leading zero, three decimals,
# "< .001". The kable() wrapper below applies it to p-value columns, found by
# header, and to all cells of p-value matrix tables, found by caption. Cell
# styling and any * significance marker are kept.
fmt_p_value <- function(p) {
  ifelse(is.na(p), NA_character_,
         ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p))))
}

format_p_cells <- function(x) {
  pat <- "(^|>|\\*\\*)\\s*([0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+(?:[eE]-?[0-9]+)?)(\\*{0,3})\\s*(<|\\*\\*|$)"
  vapply(as.character(x), function(cell) {
    if (is.na(cell) || !grepl(pat, cell, perl = TRUE)) return(cell)
    hit <- regmatches(cell, regexec(pat, cell, perl = TRUE))[[1]]
    sub(hit[1], paste0(hit[2], fmt_p_value(as.numeric(hit[3])), hit[4], hit[5]),
        cell, fixed = TRUE)
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

kable <- function(x, ..., col.names = NA, caption = NULL) {
  if (is.data.frame(x) || is.matrix(x)) {
    headers <- if (length(col.names) == ncol(x)) col.names else colnames(x)
    headers <- gsub("<[^>]+>", "", as.character(headers))
    is_p <- grepl("^p$|^p[ _.(]|_p$|\\bp \\(|\\(FDR", headers) &
      !grepl("^Sig|^Lost|family", headers)
    if (!is.null(caption) &&
        grepl("^(FDR-adjusted p-values|P-values FDR-corrected)", caption)) {
      is_p <- rep(TRUE, ncol(x))
    }
    for (k in which(is_p)) {
      # With escape = FALSE a bare "<" would be raw HTML, so write it as &lt;.
      cells <- format_p_cells(if (is.matrix(x)) x[, k] else x[[k]])
      if (identical(list(...)$escape, FALSE) && knitr::is_html_output()) {
        cells <- gsub("< .001", "&lt; .001", cells, fixed = TRUE)
      }
      if (is.matrix(x)) {
        storage.mode(x) <- "character"
        x[, k] <- cells
      } else {
        x[[k]] <- cells
      }
    }
  }
  knitr::kable(x, col.names = col.names, caption = caption, ...)
}

apa_table <- function(kbl, full_width = FALSE) {
  kableExtra::kable_classic(kbl, full_width = full_width, html_font = "Times New Roman")
}

# Consistent color palette so the same category gets the same color in
# every figure it appears in. Resting/SOS-Task and the biomarkers are
# user-specified brand colors; the 4 within-task conditions keep their

# tnf_alpha_label built via intToUtf8() and re-tagged as UTF-8, same fix as
# the delta/beta symbols in the timing-status-forest chunk -- under this
# session's "C" locale, a literal "α" in source can be misread by
# ggplot/grid's text-rendering path even though it displays fine in HTML
# tables, which silently drops that legend entry. Reused everywhere the
# TNF-alpha label is needed so every occurrence is guaranteed byte-identical.
tnf_alpha_label <- paste0("TNF-", {x <- intToUtf8(945); Encoding(x) <- "UTF-8"; x})

# APA style: italicize non-Greek statistical symbols in table headers (t, df,
# p, n, N, r, b, M, SD, SE, W, F, d); Greek-letter symbols (e.g. chi-sq) are
# left as plain text. Requires escape = FALSE on the enclosing kable() call.
italicize_stats <- function(labels) {
  stat_tokens <- c("df", "SE", "SD", "p", "t", "n", "N", "r", "b", "M", "W", "F", "d")
  for (tok in stat_tokens) {
    pattern <- paste0("(?<![A-Za-z])", tok, "(?![A-Za-z])")
    labels  <- gsub(pattern, paste0("<em>", tok, "</em>"), labels, perl = TRUE)
  }
  labels
}

```{r load-data, echo=FALSE}
# TAG003 and TAG102 declined the MRI scan and did not complete the session
# (TAG003 has T1 only, TAG102 has T1-T2 only, across all three biomarker
# panels -- consistent with stopping before the scan/task-driven timepoints).
# TAG030/TAG038/TAG046/TAG047 are pilot sessions (the 4 earliest sessions in
# the entire dataset) excluded for saliva-collection timing problems. All 6
# are excluded from the biomarker analytic sample entirely, at the source, so
# every downstream table/test (which all scope to the biomarker panels'
# SampleIDs) reflects the true N = 72.
sos_session_excluded_ids <- c(
  "TAG003", "TAG102",                     # declined MRI, did not complete the session
  "TAG030", "TAG038", "TAG046", "TAG047"  # pilot sessions, excluded for saliva-timing issues
  # (TAG030: T3/T4 saliva timestamps missing; TAG038: T4 missing; TAG046: T4
  # anomalously early relative to everyone else; TAG047: all of T2-T4 missing)
)

sos_cytokines <- read.csv(file.path(
  data_path,
  "TAG/data/SOS/saliva/Cleaned_datasets/SOS_cytokines_cleaned.csv"
)) |>
  filter(!(SampleID %in% sos_session_excluded_ids))
sos_crp <- read.csv(file.path(
  data_path,
  "TAG/data/SOS/saliva/Cleaned_datasets/SOS_CRP_cleaned.csv"
)) |>
  filter(!(SampleID %in% sos_session_excluded_ids))
sos_hormones <- read.csv(file.path(
  data_path,
  "TAG/data/SOS/saliva/Cleaned_datasets/SOS_hormones_cleaned.csv"
)) |>
  select(-starts_with("Estradiol")) |>
  filter(!(SampleID %in% sos_session_excluded_ids))

# Panel selects + the canonical analytic-sample ID list, computed immediately
# after the three raw panels load (rather than down in biomarker-processing,
# where this used to live) so that EVERY other data frame in this document --
# including ones loaded earlier in this very chunk, like sos_subj_stress --
# can scope to the exact same analytic sample via one object, biomarker_ids,
# instead of each re-deriving its own filter against sos_session_excluded_ids.
# This is the single definition of the N=72 analytic sample used everywhere
# else in the document (age_df's semi_join included).
sos_crp_panel       <- sos_crp       |> select(SampleID, Time, CRP_log)
sos_cytokines_panel <- sos_cytokines |> select(SampleID, Time, IL10_log, IL6_log, TNFalpha_log)
sos_hormones_panel  <- sos_hormones  |> select(SampleID, Time, DHEA_log, Testosterone_log, Cortisol_log)
biomarker_ids <- bind_rows(sos_crp_panel, sos_cytokines_panel, sos_hormones_panel) |>
  distinct(SampleID) |>
  pull(SampleID)

# Sample-scope check (Task 2): every data frame used in an analysis or
# descriptive table gets registered here, right after it's built, via
# check_sample_scope(). If any registered frame contains an ID outside
# biomarker_ids, this stops the render immediately, at the point where that
# frame is created -- not silently, and not deferred to the end of the
# document. A full table of every checked frame and its n is printed in the
# Sample-Scope Check section near the end of Sample Descriptives below (the
# earliest point by which every frame used in any descriptive table has been
# loaded and checked); any frame loaded later in the document for a specific
# Aim (sos_puberty, bmi, etc.) is still checked the moment it's created --
# this table is simply where the running tally is reported, not where
# enforcement happens.
sample_scope_registry <- list()
check_sample_scope <- function(df, name, id_col = "SampleID") {
  ids <- df[[id_col]]
  ids <- ids[!is.na(ids)]
  out_of_scope <- setdiff(unique(ids), biomarker_ids)
  if (length(out_of_scope) > 0) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "Sample-scope violation in %s: %d ID(s) outside the N=72 analytic sample: %s",
      name, length(out_of_scope), paste(out_of_scope, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }
  sample_scope_registry[[name]] <<- length(unique(ids))
  invisible(df)
}

# Sample timing: parse HH:MM → minutes since midnight; compute elapsed from T1.
# Moved up from the covariate-load chunk (where it originally lived alongside
# bmi/wake_time) so it's available to the AUCi sensitivity analysis below,
# which needs per-participant elapsed times well before the Sample Timing
# section later in the document.
parse_hhmm <- function(x) {
  x     <- trimws(x)
  parts <- strsplit(x, ":")
  hrs   <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sapply(parts, `[`, 1)))
  mins  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sapply(parts, function(p) if (length(p) >= 2) p[2] else "0")))
  mins[is.na(mins)] <- 0
  ifelse(nzchar(x) & !is.na(hrs), hrs * 60 + mins, NA_real_)
}

saliva_timing <- sos_saliva_times |>
  rename(SampleID = TAG.ID) |>
  mutate(
    SampleID = case_when(
      SampleID == "SOS068" ~ "TAG068",
      SampleID == "SOS076" ~ "TAG076",
      .default = SampleID
    ),
    t1_min = parse_hhmm(X1i_start),
    t2_min = parse_hhmm(X2i_start),
    t3_min = parse_hhmm(X3i_start),
    t4_min = parse_hhmm(X4i_start),
    elapsed_T2 = t2_min - t1_min,
    elapsed_T3 = t3_min - t1_min,
    elapsed_T4 = t4_min - t1_min
  ) |>
  filter(SampleID %in% biomarker_ids) |>
  select(SampleID, t1_min, elapsed_T2, elapsed_T3, elapsed_T4)
check_sample_scope(saliva_timing, "saliva_timing")

# Wake time × hormones: parse free-text wake time; join to T1 start time.
# Moved up from the covariate-load chunk (alongside saliva_timing above) so
# the AUCi diurnal-rhythm check below can use hours_since_wake, not just
# session clock time -- wake time is the more standard basis for expressing
# circadian position, since two participants starting at the same clock time
# can be at very different points on their own cortisol decline curve if they
# woke up at different times.
parse_wake <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(tolower(x))
  x <- gsub("\\s+", " ", x)
  pm <- grepl("pm", x)
  x  <- gsub("[^0-9:]", "", x)
  parts <- strsplit(x, ":")
  hrs   <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sapply(parts, `[`, 1)))
  mins  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sapply(parts, function(p) if (length(p) >= 2) p[2] else "0")))
  mins[is.na(mins)] <- 0
  hrs[pm & hrs < 12] <- hrs[pm & hrs < 12] + 12
  ifelse(is.na(hrs), NA_real_, hrs * 60 + mins)
}

wake_time <- sos_session_runner |>
  select(saliva_1, saliva_2) |>
  setNames(c("SampleID", "wake_raw")) |>
  filter(grepl("^(TAG|SOS)\\d{3}", SampleID)) |>
  mutate(
    SampleID = sub("^SOS", "TAG", SampleID),
    wake_min = parse_wake(wake_raw),
    wake_min = ifelse(wake_min > 840, NA_real_, wake_min)  # exclude implausible (>2pm)
  ) |>
  filter(SampleID %in% biomarker_ids) |>
  # sos_session_runner has 1 duplicate SampleID after the format filter
  # above (TAG017: one valid response and one blank) -- almost certainly a
  # re-submitted Qualtrics entry. (A second blank re-submission, apparently
  # meant for TAG085, was logged as "TAGS085" and is already dropped by the
  # TAG\d{3}/SOS\d{3} format filter above, so TAG085 passes through here
  # with its one valid row untouched.) Left undeduplicated, TAG017's extra
  # row would fan out through any downstream join with wake_time, silently
  # double-counting that person. Keep the row with a valid wake_min where
  # one exists.
  group_by(SampleID) |>
  slice_max(order_by = !is.na(wake_min), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(SampleID, wake_min) |>
  left_join(saliva_timing |> select(SampleID, t1_min), by = "SampleID") |>
  mutate(
    hours_since_wake = (t1_min - wake_min) / 60
  )
check_sample_scope(wake_time, "wake_time")

    data.frame(

```{r biomarker-processing, echo=FALSE}
# sos_crp_panel/sos_cytokines_panel/sos_hormones_panel/biomarker_ids now
# computed in load-data above (needed earlier, by sos_subj_stress et al.).
# Fits outcome ~ time_term with each random-effects structure in turn, stopping
# at the first non-singular fit. Same rule as run_mlm_cov() in the supplement:
# full structure, then random intercept + linear slope, then random intercept.
fit_nonsingular <- function(outcome, time_term, re_terms, data) {
  for (re_term in re_terms) {
    f   <- as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ 1 +", time_term, "+", re_term))
    fit <- lmer(f, na.action = na.omit, REML = TRUE, data = data)
    if (!isSingular(fit, tol = 1e-4)) break
  }
  fit
}

re_structure <- function(fit) deparse(lme4::findbars(formula(fit))[[1]])

run_mlm <- function(outcome, data) {
  re_full <- "(1 + poly(Time, 2) | SampleID)"
  re_lin  <- "(1 + Time | SampleID)"
  re_int  <- "(1 | SampleID)"
  mlm_lin  <- fit_nonsingular(outcome, "Time", c(re_lin, re_int), data)
  mlm_quad <- fit_nonsingular(outcome, "poly(Time, 2)", c(re_full, re_lin, re_int), data)
  # Linear comparator for the LRT. With the full quadratic structure this is
  # the usual (1 + Time | SampleID) model. If the quadratic model was
  # simplified, the comparator uses that same structure, so the LRT is a 1-df
  # test of the fixed quadratic term. It can be singular itself, which doesn't
  # affect the LRT, so it is not simplified further.
  re_quad <- paste0("(", re_structure(mlm_quad), ")")
  re_cmp  <- if (re_quad == re_full) re_lin else re_quad
  mlm_lrt_lin <- lmer(as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ 1 + Time +", re_cmp)),
                      na.action = na.omit, REML = TRUE, data = data)
  # AIC/BIC use ML refits: REML likelihoods aren't comparable across models with
  # different fixed effects. They compare the same two models as the LRT
  # (lrt_linear vs. quadratic). `linear` is the step-down fit reported in the
  # linear-only tables, which can differ from lrt_linear (IL-10).
  mlm_cmp_ml  <- lme4::refitML(mlm_lrt_lin)
  mlm_quad_ml <- lme4::refitML(mlm_quad)
  list(linear = mlm_lin, quadratic = mlm_quad, lrt_linear = mlm_lrt_lin,
       aic = AIC(mlm_cmp_ml, mlm_quad_ml), bic = BIC(mlm_cmp_ml, mlm_quad_ml))
}

re_label <- function(fit) {
  switch(re_structure(fit),
    "1 + poly(Time, 2) | SampleID" = "Full",
    "1 + Time | SampleID"          = "Intercept + linear slope",
    "1 | SampleID"                 = "Intercept only"
  )
}

# Prints a table note when a model was simplified, read from the fitted model
# so the note can't drift from what was actually estimated.
cat_re_note <- function(fit, full_structure = "1 + poly(Time, 2) | SampleID") {
  fitted_structure <- re_structure(fit)
  if (fitted_structure == full_structure) return(invisible(NULL))
  re_desc <- if (fitted_structure == "1 + Time | SampleID") {
    "a random intercept and random linear slope"
  } else {
    "a random intercept only"
  }
  cat("\n\n*Note.* The full random-effects structure was singular, so this model uses ",
      re_desc, ". The fixed-effects terms are the same as in the other models.\n\n", sep = "")
}

mlm_crp      <- run_mlm("CRP_log",          sos_crp_panel)
mlm_il10     <- run_mlm("IL10_log",         sos_cytokines_panel)
mlm_il6      <- run_mlm("IL6_log",          sos_cytokines_panel)
mlm_tnfalpha <- run_mlm("TNFalpha_log",     sos_cytokines_panel)
mlm_dhea     <- run_mlm("DHEA_log",         sos_hormones_panel)
mlm_test     <- run_mlm("Testosterone_log", sos_hormones_panel)

```{r peaks-processing, echo=FALSE}
sos_crp_wide <- sos_crp_panel |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Time,
    values_from = CRP_log,
    names_glue = "CRP_log_{Time}",
    values_fn = mean
  ) |>
  mutate(crp_peak = if_else(CRP_log_3 > CRP_log_4, CRP_log_3, CRP_log_4))

sos_cytokines_wide <- sos_cytokines_panel |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Time,
    values_from = c(IL10_log, IL6_log, TNFalpha_log),
    values_fn = mean
  ) |>
  mutate(
    il10_peak = if_else(IL10_log_3 > IL10_log_4, IL10_log_3, IL10_log_4),
    il6_peak = if_else(IL6_log_3 > IL6_log_4, IL6_log_3, IL6_log_4),
    tnfa_peak = if_else(
      TNFalpha_log_3 > TNFalpha_log_4,
      TNFalpha_log_3,
      TNFalpha_log_4
    )
  )

sos_hormones_wide <- sos_hormones_panel |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Time,
    values_from = c(DHEA_log, Testosterone_log, Cortisol_log),
    values_fn = mean
  ) |>
  mutate(
    dhea_peak = if_else(DHEA_log_3 > DHEA_log_4, DHEA_log_3, DHEA_log_4),
    test_peak = if_else(
      Testosterone_log_3 > Testosterone_log_4,
      Testosterone_log_3,
      Testosterone_log_4
    ),
    cort_peak = if_else(
      Cortisol_log_3 > Cortisol_log_4,
      Cortisol_log_3,
      Cortisol_log_4
    )
  )

make_peak_long <- function(wide_data, t1_col, peak_col, value_name) {
  wide_data |>
    select(SampleID, all_of(c(t1_col, peak_col))) |>
    pivot_longer(
      all_of(c(t1_col, peak_col)),
      names_to = "time_point",
      values_to = value_name
    ) |>
    mutate(
      time_point = factor(
        time_point,
        levels = c(t1_col, peak_col),
        labels = c("T1", "T3/T4 peak")
      )
    )
}

fmt_p_fdr   <- function(p) {
  if (p < 0.001) "italic(p)[FDR] < 0.001" else paste0("italic(p)[FDR] == ", round(p, 4))
}
fmt_p_plain <- function(p) {
  if (p < 0.001) "p < 0.001" else sprintf("p = %.3f", p)
}
# Used for the HR figure annotations below, which show FDR-corrected p (the
# HR paired t-tests are now FDR-corrected within their 4-test family, same
# as the prose) -- labeled distinctly from fmt_p_plain's "p =" so the figure
# doesn't look like it's showing a raw, uncorrected value.
fmt_p_fdr_plain <- function(p) {
  if (p < 0.001) "italic(p)[FDR] < .001" else paste0("italic(p)[FDR] == ", sub("^0\\.", ".", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
}
# Moved up from the (old) Aim 1b/HR chunk so it's available to the Aim
# 1a Subjective Stress results paragraph too, now that Aim 1a runs before HR.
fmt_p_txt <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", paste0("= ", round(p, 3)))

biomarker_plot <- function(data, y_col, y_label, p_fdr) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = time_point, y = .data[[y_col]])) +
    stat_halfeye(
      aes(fill = time_point),
      adjust = 0.5,
      width = 0.6,
      .width = 0,
      justification = -0.2,
      point_colour = NA
    ) +
    geom_boxplot(
      width = 0.15,
      outlier.shape = NA,
      color = "gray30",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
      aes(color = time_point),
      position = position_jitter(seed = 1, width = 0.1),
      size = 1.2,
      alpha = 0.3
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "C", begin = 0.2, end = 0.85) +
    scale_color_viridis_d(option = "C", begin = 0.2, end = 0.85, guide = "none") +
    geom_signif(
      comparisons = list(c("T1", "T3/T4 peak")),
      annotations = fmt_p_fdr(p_fdr),
      textsize = 3.5,
      vjust = 0.1,
      tip_length = 0.02,
      parse = TRUE
    ) +
    ylab(y_label) +
    xlab(NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 5, b = 5, l = 5))
}

summarize_se <- function(
  data,
  measure_var,
  group_vars = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  conf.interval = 0.95
) {
  data |>
    group_by(across(all_of(group_vars))) |>
    summarise(
      n = sum(!is.na(.data[[measure_var]])),
      # sd before mean: the mean overwrites measure_var within summarise(), so
      # sd() computed after it sees one value per group and returns NA.
      sd = sd(.data[[measure_var]], na.rm = na.rm),
      !!measure_var := mean(.data[[measure_var]], na.rm = na.rm),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(se = sd / sqrt(n), ci = se * qt(conf.interval / 2 + 0.5, n - 1))
}

summary_subj <- summarize_se(
  subj_stress_long,
  measure_var = "stress",
  group_vars = "condition",
  na.rm = TRUE
)

wt_plt_sc_sd  <- wilcox.test(sos_subj_stress$selfconnected_subj_stress,

                              alternative = "two.sided", paired = TRUE)
wt_plt_sc_oth <- wilcox.test(sos_subj_stress$selfconnected_subj_stress,
                              sos_subj_stress$other_subj_stress,
                              alternative = "two.sided", paired = TRUE)
wt_plt_sd_oth <- wilcox.test(sos_subj_stress$selfdisconnected_subj_stress,

# FDR-corrected within this 3-test family (computed here, immediately after

# down both use these same values rather than the plot showing raw p while
# the table/prose show FDR-corrected p).
subj_wilcoxon_pfdr <- setNames(
  p.adjust(c(wt_plt_sc_sd$p.value, wt_plt_sc_oth$p.value, wt_plt_sd_oth$p.value), method = "fdr"),
  c("sc_sd", "sc_oth", "sd_oth")
)

subj_comparisons <- list(

  c("You Watch You", "Both Watch Peer")
)

      fmt_p_fdr_plain(subj_wilcoxon_pfdr["sc_oth"]),
      fmt_p_fdr_plain(subj_wilcoxon_pfdr["sd_oth"])
    ),
    tip_length = 0.02, vjust = -0.4, textsize = 4, y_position = c(3.5, 4.5, 4),

  ) +

# Data Processing

## Winsorized Values

Counts of winsorized values in the biomarker data used in every analysis. A value counts as winsorized when its `*_log` value in the cleaned file differs from the natural log of its raw concentration.

```{r winsorized-counts}
saliva_clean_path <- file.path(data_path, "TAG/data/SOS/saliva/Cleaned_datasets")
winsor_raw <- list(
  hormones  = read.csv(file.path(saliva_clean_path, "SOS_hormones_cleaned.csv")),
  crp       = read.csv(file.path(saliva_clean_path, "SOS_CRP_cleaned.csv")),
  cytokines = read.csv(file.path(saliva_clean_path, "SOS_cytokines_cleaned.csv"))
)

count_winsorized <- function(label, df, raw_col, log_col) {
  diff_ln <- df[[log_col]] - log(df[[raw_col]])
  changed <- !is.na(diff_ln) & abs(diff_ln) > 1e-6
  in_sample <- df$SampleID %in% biomarker_ids
  dropped   <- df$SampleID %in% sos_session_excluded_ids
  tibble(
    Biomarker = label,
    n_values  = sum(!is.na(df[[log_col]]) & in_sample),
    lower     = sum(changed & in_sample & diff_ln > 0),
    upper     = sum(changed & in_sample & diff_ln < 0),
    people    = n_distinct(df$SampleID[changed & in_sample]),
    excluded  = sum(changed & dropped)
  )
}

bind_rows(
  count_winsorized("CRP",          winsor_raw$crp,       "CRP_Ave",            "CRP_log"),
  count_winsorized("IL-10",        winsor_raw$cytokines, "IL10_Ave",           "IL10_log"),
  count_winsorized("IL-6",         winsor_raw$cytokines, "IL6_Ave",            "IL6_log"),
  count_winsorized("TNF-α",        winsor_raw$cytokines, "TNFalpha_Ave",       "TNFalpha_log"),
  count_winsorized("DHEA",         winsor_raw$hormones,  "DHEA_pg_mL",         "DHEA_log"),
  count_winsorized("Testosterone", winsor_raw$hormones,  "Testosterone_pg_mL", "Testosterone_log"),
  count_winsorized("Cortisol",     winsor_raw$hormones,  "Cortisol_ug_dL",     "Cortisol_log")
) |>
  kable(col.names = c("Biomarker", "Values (N = 72)", "Lower-limit winsorized (N = 72)",
                      "Upper-limit winsorized (N = 72)", "Participants affected (N = 72)",
                      "Winsorized values from excluded participants"),
        caption = "Winsorized values by biomarker") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

*Note.* The methods document reports lower-limit winsorizing only (DHEA n = 4, testosterone n = 4, cortisol n = 1). Those counts include one DHEA value from an excluded pilot participant (TAG047). The upper-limit values are not described there. Winsorizing was done upstream of the cleaned files, so this report uses the values as supplied.

# Sample Descriptives

## Age

```{r age-descriptives}
# Age at session (also reused as age_df in the Aim 2 puberty-load chunk)
dob_session_raw <- read.csv(file.path(
  data_path, "SOS/SOS-study-monash/questionnaires/SOS_DOB_sessiondate.csv"
)) |>
  mutate(SampleID = sub("_", "", subject_spit_id))

age_df <- dob_session_raw |>
  filter(redcap_event_name == "ongoing_records_arm_1") |>
  select(SampleID, dob) |>
  mutate(dob = as.Date(lubridate::parse_date_time(dob, orders = c("ymd", "mdy")))) |>
  inner_join(
    dob_session_raw |>
      filter(redcap_event_name == "sos_arm_1") |>
      select(SampleID, sos_session_date) |>
      mutate(sos_session_date = as.Date(lubridate::parse_date_time(sos_session_date, orders = c("ymd", "mdy")))),
    by = "SampleID"
  ) |>
  mutate(age_at_session = as.numeric(sos_session_date - dob) / 365.25) |>
  select(SampleID, age_at_session) |>
  # Scoped to the analytic sample via biomarker_ids (N=72; see load-data
  # above -- this is the single definition of the analytic sample, also used
  # to scope sos_subj_stress, dep, bfnes/gender, etc.). Without this, age_df
  # pulls anyone merely logged/scheduled for an SOS visit in REDCap
  # (ongoing_records_arm_1 x sos_arm_1), which includes people with no
  # biomarker or questionnaire data at all (likely no-shows/incomplete
  # sessions) and inflates n well beyond the analytic sample. This join is
  # not a duplicate-row bug — both REDCap event filters were checked and
  # have zero duplicate SampleIDs — it's a sample-scope mismatch.
  # Note: this scoping still only recovers 71 of the 72 analytic-sample
  # participants with any DOB/session-date record at all -- TAG122 has none
  # in SOS_DOB_sessiondate.csv -- and of those 71, TAG313 has a blank dob
  # field that computes to NA age, leaving n = 70 with a valid computed age.
  semi_join(
    tibble(SampleID = biomarker_ids),
    by = "SampleID"
  )
check_sample_scope(age_df, "age_df")

age_df |>
  summarise(
    n    = sum(!is.na(age_at_session)),
    Mean = round(mean(age_at_session, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD   = round(sd(age_at_session,   na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Min  = round(min(age_at_session,  na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Max  = round(max(age_at_session,  na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Age at session (years)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r age-distribution}
age_df |>
  filter(!is.na(age_at_session)) |>
  mutate(age_bin = cut(age_at_session,
                        breaks = seq(floor(min(age_at_session)), ceiling(max(age_at_session)), by = 1),
                        right = FALSE)) |>
  count(age_bin, name = "n") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Age (years)", "n", "%")),
        caption = "Distribution of age at session") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

## Sample-Scope Check

Every data frame registered via `check_sample_scope()` so far (defined near the top of load-data, right after `biomarker_ids`; enforced at each frame's creation point throughout the document, so the render fails immediately if any frame contains an ID outside the N=72 analytic sample). Frames loaded later, for a specific Aim (e.g. `sos_puberty`, `bmi`), are checked the moment they're created and folded into this same registry; see the final Sample-Scope Check Addendum near the end of the document for the complete, final table.

```{r sample-scope-table-early}
tibble(
  `Data frame` = names(sample_scope_registry),
  n = unlist(sample_scope_registry, use.names = FALSE)
) |>
  kable(caption = "Sample-scope registry (data frames checked so far; n = distinct in-scope SampleIDs)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

## Race and Ethnicity

*Race/ethnicity was collected as part of the broader TAG study (not the SOS-specific protocol), so
coverage is incomplete for the newer SOS-specific recruits (SampleIDs >= TAG300), most of whom were
not enrolled during the TAG wave when this questionnaire was administered. Race is multi-select
(a participant may be flagged for more than one category), so race percentages do not sum to 100%.*

```{r race-ethnicity-descriptives, echo=FALSE}
# TAG-wide race/ethnicity data (from the broader TAG study, not SOS-specific).
# Coding: Ethnicity 1 = Hispanic/Latino, 2 = Not Hispanic/Latino; each Race_*
# column 1 = is NOT that race, 2 = IS that race; -9 = declined/missing.
race_eth_raw <- read_excel(file.path(
  data_path, "TAG/data/Demographics/Race_Ethnicity/TAG_W3_Race_Ethnicity.xlsx"
), sheet = "Wave 3 Cumulative") |>
  select(SampleID = tagid, Ethnicity, Race_NAAN, Race_Asian, Race_NHPI,
         Race_Black, Race_White, Race_Other) |>
  mutate(across(-SampleID, \(x) na_if(x, -9)))

# Two SOS-specific participants (SampleID >= TAG300) with race/ethnicity
# available from a separate SOS-specific source, not the TAG-wide file above
# (which only covers the original TAG cohort). Same coding as above.
race_eth_sos_specific <- tribble(
  ~SampleID, ~Ethnicity, ~Race_NAAN, ~Race_Asian, ~Race_NHPI, ~Race_Black, ~Race_White, ~Race_Other,
  "TAG306",  2,          1,          1,           1,          1,           2,           1,
  "TAG317",  2,          1,          1,           1,          1,           2,           1
)

race_eth_df <- bind_rows(race_eth_raw, race_eth_sos_specific) |>
  distinct(SampleID, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(SampleID %in% biomarker_ids)

n_race_missing <- length(biomarker_ids) - nrow(race_eth_df)

race_labels <- c(Race_White = "White", Race_Black = "Black", Race_Asian = "Asian",
                  Race_NHPI = "Native Hawaiian / Pacific Islander",
                  Race_NAAN = "American Indian / Alaska Native", Race_Other = "Other")

# Combined race/ethnicity reporting: each person is assigned a single race
# label (their one flagged race, "More than one race" if multiple are
# flagged, or "Race not reported" if none/unknown), then crossed with
# ethnicity (Hispanic/Latino vs. Not Hispanic/Latino) into one combined
# category, e.g. "Not Hispanic/Latino, White".
race_flags        <- as.matrix(race_eth_df[, names(race_labels)]) == 2
n_races_flagged   <- rowSums(race_flags, na.rm = TRUE)
single_race_label <- race_labels[names(race_labels)[max.col(replace(race_flags, is.na(race_flags), FALSE), ties.method = "first")]]

race_eth_combined <- race_eth_df |>
  mutate(
    ethnicity_label = case_when(
      Ethnicity == 1 ~ "Hispanic/Latino",
      Ethnicity == 2 ~ "Not Hispanic/Latino",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    race_label = case_when(
      n_races_flagged > 1  ~ "More than one race",
      n_races_flagged == 1 ~ unname(single_race_label),
      TRUE                 ~ "Race not reported"
    ),
    combined_label = if_else(is.na(ethnicity_label), NA_character_,
                              paste0(ethnicity_label, ", ", race_label))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(combined_label))

n_declined <- nrow(race_eth_df) - nrow(race_eth_combined)

race_eth_combined |>
  count(combined_label, name = "n") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / length(biomarker_ids), 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Race / Ethnicity", "n", "%")),
        caption = paste0("Combined race/ethnicity (of ", length(biomarker_ids), "-person sample; ",
                          n_race_missing, " with no race/ethnicity data on file",
                          if (n_declined > 0) paste0(", ", n_declined, " declined to answer") else "",
                          "; percentages of full sample)")) |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

# Peak Timepoint Distribution

Before the immune and hormone reactivity models (Aim 1c), we characterized *when*
each person's peak biomarker value occurred across all four saliva collection timepoints
(T1–T4), rather than restricting "peak" to T3 vs. T4 as in the reactivity analyses below.
For each biomarker, each participant is assigned the timepoint at which their
(log-transformed) concentration was highest, using whichever timepoints they have
non-missing data for. Ties (identical values at two timepoints) are broken in favor of
the earlier timepoint.

```{r peak-timepoint-processing, echo=FALSE}
peak_timepoint_counts <- function(wide_data, cols, biomarker_name) {
  wide_data |>
    select(SampleID, all_of(cols)) |>
    pivot_longer(-SampleID, names_to = "time_point", values_to = "value") |>
    filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    group_by(SampleID) |>
    slice_max(value, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(
      time_point = paste0("T", str_extract(time_point, "\\d$")),
      time_point = factor(time_point, levels = paste0("T", 1:4))
    ) |>
    count(time_point, .drop = FALSE, name = "n") |>
    mutate(biomarker = biomarker_name, pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
}

peak_timepoint_tbl <- bind_rows(
  peak_timepoint_counts(sos_crp_wide,       paste0("CRP_log_",          1:4), "CRP"),
  peak_timepoint_counts(sos_cytokines_wide, paste0("IL10_log_",         1:4), "IL-10"),
  peak_timepoint_counts(sos_cytokines_wide, paste0("IL6_log_",          1:4), "IL-6"),
  peak_timepoint_counts(sos_cytokines_wide, paste0("TNFalpha_log_",     1:4), "TNF-alpha"),
  peak_timepoint_counts(sos_hormones_wide,  paste0("DHEA_log_",         1:4), "DHEA"),
  peak_timepoint_counts(sos_hormones_wide,  paste0("Testosterone_log_", 1:4), "Testosterone"),
  peak_timepoint_counts(sos_hormones_wide,  paste0("Cortisol_log_",     1:4), "Cortisol")
) |>
  mutate(biomarker = factor(biomarker,
    levels = c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", "TNF-alpha", "DHEA", "Testosterone", "Cortisol")))
```

## Counts by Timepoint

```{r peak-timepoint-table}
peak_timepoint_tbl |>
  mutate(display = paste0(n, " (", pct, "%)")) |>
  select(biomarker, time_point, display) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = time_point, values_from = display) |>
  arrange(biomarker) |>
  # Display-only recode: the underlying factor stays "TNF-alpha" (ASCII,
  # ggplot/grid-safe for the ind-growth-curves/peak-timepoint-plot figures
  # that also key off this table), but HTML tables render the real Greek
  # alpha fine, so swap it in just for this table's text (same pattern used
  # elsewhere in this document, e.g. ind_curve_data above).
  mutate(biomarker = recode(as.character(biomarker), "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α")) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "T1", "T2", "T3", "T4")),
        caption = "Number (%) of participants whose peak (highest) value for each biomarker occurred at each timepoint") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r peak-timepoint-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Distribution of each biomarker's peak (highest) timepoint across participants"}
ggplot(peak_timepoint_tbl, aes(x = time_point, y = pct, fill = time_point)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "C", begin = 0.2, end = 0.85, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~biomarker, nrow = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Peak timepoint", y = "% of participants") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r peak-timepoint-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
peak_modal <- peak_timepoint_tbl |>
  group_by(biomarker) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

modal_sentence <- peak_modal |>
  mutate(biomarker = recode(as.character(biomarker), "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α")) |>
  mutate(txt = paste0(biomarker, " (", time_point, ": n = ", n, ", ", pct, "%)")) |>
  pull(txt) |>
  paste(collapse = "; ")
```

**Results.** The modal (most common) peak timepoint for each biomarker was: `r modal_sentence`.

# Aim 1a: Subjective Stress Reactivity

*Aim 1a (manuscript): Both Watch You Likert stress ratings vs. You Watch You and Both Watch Peer, via Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (ordinal ratings), FDR-corrected within this 3-test family.*

## Condition Means

```{r subj-condition-means}
# Computed directly from subj_stress_long, independently of summary_subj.
subj_stress_long |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  summarise(
    n    = sum(!is.na(stress)),
    Mean = round(mean(stress, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD   = round(sd(stress,   na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Condition = condition) |>
  kable(caption = "Subjective stress ratings by task condition (n = complete ratings per condition)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

## Descriptives

```{r subj-stress-descriptives}
bind_rows(
  subjective_difference |> select(-SampleID) |> summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sum(!is.na(x)))) |> mutate(stat = "n"),
  subjective_difference |> select(-SampleID) |> summarise(across(everything(), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |> mutate(stat = "Mean"),
  subjective_difference |> select(-SampleID) |> summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sd(x,   na.rm = TRUE))) |> mutate(stat = "SD")
) |>
  select(stat, everything()) |>
  rename(
    `ΔSubjective Stress: Both Watch You vs. You Watch You`    = subj_scsd_difference,
    `ΔSubjective Stress: Both Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer` = subj_scother_difference
  ) |>
  mutate(across(-stat, \(x) if_else(stat == "n", sprintf("%d", as.integer(x)), sprintf("%.3f", x)))) |>
  kable(caption = "Subjective stress difference scores (positive = higher stress during Both Watch You)")
```

## Plot

```{r subj-stress-plot, fig.width=6, fig.height=6, fig.cap="Subjective stress ratings by task condition (Both Watch You, You Watch You, `Both Watch Peer`)"}
subj_plot
```

## Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Tests

Two-tailed, paired. Reuses the same test objects (`wt_plt_sc_sd`, `wt_plt_sc_oth`, `wt_plt_sd_oth`) computed above for the plot annotations, so the displayed table, the plot, and the prose below can't drift out of sync with each other.

```{r subj-wilcoxon-table}
# FDR-corrected within this 3-test family (the three pairwise subjective-
# stress comparisons), matching the convention already used for the other
# small within-domain test families in this document (HR: 4, immune: 4,
# hormones: 3) -- previously left uncorrected while every other family was.
# Reuses subj_wilcoxon_pfdr (computed above, alongside the tests themselves)
# rather than re-running p.adjust() a second time on the same three p-values.
subj_wilcoxon_tbl <- tibble(
  Comparison = c("Both Watch You vs. You Watch You",
                  "Both Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer",
                  "You Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer"),
  # n = complete pairs actually used by each wilcox.test(paired = TRUE) call
  # above (which drops incomplete pairs via complete.cases() internally).
  n = c(
    sum(complete.cases(sos_subj_stress$selfconnected_subj_stress, sos_subj_stress$selfdisconnected_subj_stress)),
    sum(complete.cases(sos_subj_stress$selfconnected_subj_stress, sos_subj_stress$other_subj_stress)),
    sum(complete.cases(sos_subj_stress$selfdisconnected_subj_stress, sos_subj_stress$other_subj_stress))
  ),
  W     = c(wt_plt_sc_sd$statistic, wt_plt_sc_oth$statistic, wt_plt_sd_oth$statistic),
  p     = c(wt_plt_sc_sd$p.value,   wt_plt_sc_oth$p.value,   wt_plt_sd_oth$p.value),
  p_fdr = unname(subj_wilcoxon_pfdr[c("sc_sd", "sc_oth", "sd_oth")])
) |>
  mutate(across(c(p, p_fdr), \(x) round(x, 6)))

subj_wilcoxon_tbl |>
  mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = p_fdr < 0.05, color = if_else(p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(col.names = italicize_stats(c("Comparison", "n", "W", "p (raw)", "p (FDR)")), escape = FALSE,
        caption = "Wilcoxon signed-rank tests: subjective stress across task conditions") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r subj-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
subj_wide <- sos_subj_stress
m_sc  <- round(mean(subj_wide$selfconnected_subj_stress,  na.rm = TRUE), 2)
m_sd2 <- round(mean(subj_wide$selfdisconnected_subj_stress, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
m_oth <- round(mean(subj_wide$other_subj_stress,           na.rm = TRUE), 2)
sd_sc  <- round(sd(subj_wide$selfconnected_subj_stress,    na.rm = TRUE), 2)
sd_sd2 <- round(sd(subj_wide$selfdisconnected_subj_stress, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
sd_oth <- round(sd(subj_wide$other_subj_stress,            na.rm = TRUE), 2)

p_fdr_sc_sd  <- subj_wilcoxon_tbl$p_fdr[subj_wilcoxon_tbl$Comparison == "Both Watch You vs. You Watch You"]
p_fdr_sc_oth <- subj_wilcoxon_tbl$p_fdr[subj_wilcoxon_tbl$Comparison == "Both Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer"]
p_fdr_sd_oth <- subj_wilcoxon_tbl$p_fdr[subj_wilcoxon_tbl$Comparison == "You Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer"]
```

**Results.** Participants reported the highest subjective stress during the Both Watch You condition (*M* = `r m_sc`, *SD* = `r sd_sc`), relative to both the You Watch You condition (*M* = `r m_sd2`, *SD* = `r sd_sd2`; Wilcoxon *W* = `r wt_plt_sc_sd$statistic`, *p*~FDR~ `r fmt_p_txt(p_fdr_sc_sd)`) and the Both Watch Peer condition (*M* = `r m_oth`, *SD* = `r sd_oth`; Wilcoxon *W* = `r wt_plt_sc_oth$statistic`, *p*~FDR~ `r fmt_p_txt(p_fdr_sc_oth)`). The You Watch You and Both Watch Peer conditions also differed from one another (Wilcoxon *W* = `r wt_plt_sd_oth$statistic`, *p*~FDR~ `r fmt_p_txt(p_fdr_sd_oth)`). FDR-corrected within this 3-test family.

# Aim 1b: Heart Rate Reactivity

*Aim 1b (manuscript): task heart rate vs. resting-state baseline (two 5-min pre-task scans), and Both Watch You vs. You Watch You/Both Watch Peer/fixation-cross, via two-tailed paired t-tests, FDR-corrected within this 4-test family.*

## Descriptive Means

```{r hr-descriptives}
tibble(

  ),

  ), 2),

    sd(hr_all_wide$`Resting 1`),
    sd(hr_all_wide$`Resting 2`, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd(hr_all_wide$resting_avg),
    sd(hr_all_wide$Task),
    sd(pull_hr("Fixation-Cross")),
    sd(pull_hr("Both Watch Peer")),
    sd(pull_hr("You Watch You")),
    sd(pull_hr("Both Watch You"))
  ), 2)
) |>

```

## HR Difference Score Descriptives

```{r hr-diff-descriptives}
bind_rows(
  hr_difference |> select(-SampleID) |> summarise(across(everything(), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |> mutate(stat = "Mean"),
  hr_difference |> select(-SampleID) |> summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sd(x,   na.rm = TRUE))) |> mutate(stat = "SD")
) |>
  select(stat, everything()) |>

    `ΔHR: Task vs. Rest`  = task_rs_hr_diff,

  ) |>

## Paired t-tests

```{r hr-ttests}
# FDR-corrected within this 4-test family (the four HR comparisons), matching
# the convention already used for the other within-domain test families in
# this document (immune: 4, hormones: 3) -- previously left uncorrected while
# every other family was.
hr_ttest_tbl <- list(
  "Task vs. Resting" = t.test(hr_all_wide$Task, hr_all_wide$resting_avg, alternative = "two.sided", paired = TRUE),
  "Both Watch You vs. Fixation-Cross" = t.test(pull_hr("Both Watch You"), pull_hr("Fixation-Cross"), alternative = "two.sided", paired = TRUE),
  "Both Watch You vs. You Watch You" = t.test(pull_hr("Both Watch You"), pull_hr("You Watch You"), alternative = "two.sided", paired = TRUE),
  "Both Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer" = t.test(pull_hr("Both Watch You"), pull_hr("Both Watch Peer"), alternative = "two.sided", paired = TRUE)
) |>
  map(broom::tidy) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "comparison") |>
  select(comparison, estimate, statistic, parameter, p.value) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr")) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))

hr_ttest_tbl |>
  mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = p_fdr < 0.05,
    color = if_else(p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(col.names = italicize_stats(c("Comparison", "Mean diff", "t", "df", "p (raw)", "p (FDR)")), escape = FALSE,
        caption = "Paired t-tests: heart rate reactivity across task conditions (FDR-corrected within this 4-test family)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r hr-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# fmt_p_txt is now defined in the setup chunk (needed by Aim 1a Subjective too)
hr_task_rest <- hr_ttest_tbl |> filter(comparison == "Task vs. Resting")
hr_sc_sd     <- hr_ttest_tbl |> filter(comparison == "Both Watch You vs. You Watch You")
hr_sc_oth    <- hr_ttest_tbl |> filter(comparison == "Both Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer")
hr_sc_rest   <- hr_ttest_tbl |> filter(comparison == "Both Watch You vs. Fixation-Cross")
```

**Results.** Heart rate was significantly higher during the SOS task compared to the pre-task resting scan (*M*~diff~ = `r hr_task_rest$estimate` bpm, *t*(`r hr_task_rest$parameter`) = `r hr_task_rest$statistic`, *p*~FDR~ `r fmt_p_txt(hr_task_rest$p_fdr)`). Within the task, heart rate during the Both Watch You condition was significantly higher than both the You Watch You condition (*M*~diff~ = `r hr_sc_sd$estimate` bpm, *t*(`r hr_sc_sd$parameter`) = `r hr_sc_sd$statistic`, *p*~FDR~ `r fmt_p_txt(hr_sc_sd$p_fdr)`) and the Both Watch Peer condition (*M*~diff~ = `r hr_sc_oth$estimate` bpm, *t*(`r hr_sc_oth$parameter`) = `r hr_sc_oth$statistic`, *p*~FDR~ `r fmt_p_txt(hr_sc_oth$p_fdr)`), and compared to the within-task fixation-cross period (*M*~diff~ = `r hr_sc_rest$estimate` bpm, *t*(`r hr_sc_rest$parameter`) = `r hr_sc_rest$statistic`, *p*~FDR~ `r fmt_p_txt(hr_sc_rest$p_fdr)`). FDR-corrected within this 4-test family.

# Aim 1c: Salivary Biomarkers — Time Trends

*Aim 1c (manuscript): "We estimated both the linear and quadratic effects of time point on each immune and hormone biomarker using a random intercept and a random effect of time point nested within participants."*

## Model Comparison (AIC / BIC)

```{r model-comparison}
mlm_list <- list(
  CRP = mlm_crp, `IL-10` = mlm_il10, `IL-6` = mlm_il6, `TNF-alpha` = mlm_tnfalpha,
  DHEA = mlm_dhea, Testosterone = mlm_test, Cortisol = mlm_cort
)

lrt_tbl <- imap_dfr(mlm_list, function(res, name) {
  a       <- anova(res$lrt_linear, res$quadratic, refit = TRUE)
  p_col   <- grep("Pr", colnames(a), value = TRUE)[1]
  # The LRT and AIC/BIC must be comparing the same two models.
  stopifnot(a$Df[2] == diff(res$aic$df))
  tibble(
    biomarker = recode(name, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α"),  # display-only; see model-comparison above
    chisq   = round(a$Chisq[2], 2),
    # Df = 4 when the quadratic model keeps (1 + poly(Time,2) | SampleID): that
    # term adds a random quadratic slope and its covariances with the
    # intercept/linear random slopes, on top of the 1 new fixed (quadratic)
    # term, so the LRT is not a clean test of the fixed effect alone. Df = 1
    # when that structure was singular: both models then share the simplified
    # random effects (see run_mlm), so the LRT tests the fixed term alone.
    df      = a$Df[2],
    p_raw   = as.numeric(a[2, p_col])
  )
}) |>
  mutate(
    group = c(rep("Immune", 4), rep("Hormones", 3)),
    p_fdr = c(
      p.adjust(p_raw[1:4], method = "fdr"),
      p.adjust(p_raw[5:7], method = "fdr")
    )
  )

model_comp_tbl <- imap_dfr(mlm_list, function(res, name) {
  tibble(
    # Display-only recode: mlm_list's own name stays ASCII "TNF-alpha" (it's
    # also used as a ggplot facet/panel-lookup key elsewhere in this
    # document, where a literal alpha can garble under this session's "C"
    # locale), but this derived table is text/HTML-only, so show the real
    # Greek alpha here.
    biomarker = recode(name, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α"),
    Model   = c("Linear", "Quadratic"),
    random_effects = c(re_label(res$lrt_linear), re_label(res$quadratic)),
    df      = res$aic$df,
    AIC     = round(res$aic$AIC, 1),
    BIC     = round(res$bic$BIC, 1)
  )
})

best_rows <- model_comp_tbl |>
  group_by(biomarker) |>
  mutate(is_best = BIC == min(BIC)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pull(is_best)

# Linear-only tables whose step-down fit isn't the model compared here.
lin_differs <- names(mlm_list)[map_lgl(mlm_list, \(res) re_structure(res$linear) != re_structure(res$lrt_linear))]
lin_differs <- recode(lin_differs, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α")

model_comp_tbl |>
  left_join(lrt_tbl |> select(biomarker, chisq, lrt_df = df, p_fdr), by = "biomarker") |>
  mutate(
    chisq  = if_else(Model == "Quadratic", sprintf("%.2f", chisq), ""),
    lrt_df = if_else(Model == "Quadratic", as.character(lrt_df), ""),
    p_fdr  = if_else(Model == "Quadratic", fmt_p_value(p_fdr), "")
  ) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "Model", "Random effects", "df", "AIC", "BIC",
                                      "chi-sq", "LRT df", "p (FDR)")),
        caption = "Model comparison: linear vs. quadratic time trend, by biomarker (ML fits; lowest BIC in bold; LRT FDR-corrected within immune and hormone groups)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE) |>
  row_spec(which(best_rows), bold = TRUE, color = "#2166ac")
```

*Note.* AIC, BIC, and the likelihood ratio test (LRT) compare the same two ML-refit models for each biomarker. Where the quadratic model kept the full random-effects structure, its comparator has a random intercept and linear slope, and the LRT has 4 df because it also tests the random quadratic terms. Where the quadratic model was simplified, its comparator has the same random effects, so the LRT has 1 df and tests the fixed quadratic term alone. `r if (length(lin_differs) > 0) paste0("For ", paste(lin_differs, collapse = ", "), ", that comparator is singular and is kept so the two models share random effects; the linear-only fixed-effects table instead reports the step-down fit (random intercept only).")`

A significant LRT indicates that adding the quadratic time term significantly improves model fit.

```{r model-lrt}
lrt_tbl |>
  mutate(
    p_raw_disp = round(p_raw, 4),
    p_fdr_disp = cell_spec(round(p_fdr, 4), bold = p_fdr < 0.05,
      color = if_else(p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))
  ) |>
  select(biomarker, group, chisq, df, p_raw_disp, p_fdr_disp) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "Group", "chi-sq", "df", "p (raw)", "p (FDR)")),
        caption = "Likelihood ratio test: quadratic vs. linear (FDR-corrected within immune and hormone groups; bold = p (FDR) < .05). Df = 4 where the quadratic model keeps its full random-effects structure, so the test also includes the random quadratic terms. Df = 1 where that structure was singular and both models use the same simplified random effects, so the test is of the fixed quadratic term alone.") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r biomarker-trends-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
best_model_tbl <- model_comp_tbl |>
  group_by(biomarker) |>
  slice_min(BIC, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()
n_quad <- sum(best_model_tbl$Model == "Quadratic")
n_lin  <- sum(best_model_tbl$Model == "Linear")
quad_biomarkers <- best_model_tbl |> filter(Model == "Quadratic") |> pull(biomarker) |> paste(collapse = ", ")
lin_biomarkers  <- best_model_tbl |> filter(Model == "Linear")    |> pull(biomarker) |> paste(collapse = ", ")

n_lrt_sig     <- sum(lrt_tbl$p_fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
lrt_sig_names <- lrt_tbl |> filter(p_fdr < 0.05) |> pull(biomarker) |> paste(collapse = ", ")
lrt_ns_names  <- lrt_tbl |> filter(p_fdr >= 0.05) |> pull(biomarker) |> paste(collapse = ", ")

# Which criteria favor the quadratic model, per biomarker. |delta BIC| < 1 is
# labeled essentially tied; this is descriptive only.
aic_quad_names <- model_comp_tbl |>
  group_by(biomarker) |> slice_min(AIC, n = 1) |> ungroup() |>
  filter(Model == "Quadratic") |> pull(biomarker)
fit_criteria_text <- model_comp_tbl |>
  select(biomarker, Model, AIC, BIC) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = c(AIC, BIC)) |>
  left_join(lrt_tbl |> select(biomarker, p_fdr), by = "biomarker") |>
  mutate(
    bic_diff = BIC_Quadratic - BIC_Linear,
    criteria = pmap_chr(
      list(AIC_Quadratic < AIC_Linear, bic_diff <= -1, p_fdr < .05, abs(bic_diff) < 1),
      function(aic, bic, lrt, tied) {
        crit <- c("AIC", "BIC", "LRT")[c(aic, bic, lrt)]
        txt  <- if (length(crit) == 0) "none" else paste(crit, collapse = ", ")
        if (tied) paste0(txt, "; BIC essentially tied") else txt
      }
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(txt = paste0(biomarker, " (", criteria, ")")) |>
  pull(txt) |>
  paste(collapse = "; ")
```

**Results.** We modeled log-transformed biomarker concentrations across four timepoints (T1–T4) using linear mixed models. BIC, the primary model-fit criterion, was lowest for the quadratic model for `r n_quad` of 7 biomarkers (`r quad_biomarkers`)`r if (n_lin > 0) paste0(", with a linear trajectory preferred for ", lin_biomarkers)`. AIC was lowest for the quadratic model for `r length(aic_quad_names)` of 7 biomarkers (`r paste(aic_quad_names, collapse = ", ")`). Likelihood ratio tests (quadratic vs. linear) were FDR-corrected within immune markers and hormones separately; the quadratic term significantly improved fit for `r n_lrt_sig` biomarker`r if (n_lrt_sig != 1) "s"``r if (n_lrt_sig > 0) paste0(" (", lrt_sig_names, ")")``r if (nchar(lrt_ns_names) > 0) paste0("; the improvement was not significant for ", lrt_ns_names)`. The criteria supporting a quadratic trajectory for each biomarker were: `r fit_criteria_text` (BIC is labeled essentially tied when the two models differ by less than 1). Fixed effects are shown below with FDR-corrected p-values within each term across immune markers and hormones separately.

## Fixed Effects: Quadratic Models {.tabset}

```{r quad-fixed-effects, results='asis'}
# Collect all fixed effects, then FDR-correct within term × group
all_fixed_effects <- imap_dfr(mlm_list, function(res, name) {
  broom.mixed::tidy(res$quadratic, effects = "fixed") |>
    mutate(biomarker = name)
}) |>
  mutate(group = if_else(
    biomarker %in% c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", "TNF-alpha"), "Immune", "Hormones"
  )) |>
  group_by(term, group) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr")) |>
  ungroup()

iwalk(mlm_list, function(res, name) {
  # name itself stays ASCII "TNF-alpha" (used below to filter
  # all_fixed_effects, which is also keyed on that literal); display_name is
  # recoded to the real Greek alpha for the heading/caption text only.
  display_name <- recode(name, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α")
  cat("\n\n### ", display_name, "\n\n")
  tbl <- all_fixed_effects |>
    filter(biomarker == name) |>
    select(term, estimate, std.error, statistic, df, p.value, p_fdr) |>
    mutate(
      across(c(estimate, std.error, statistic, df), \(x) round(x, 3)),
      p.value = round(p.value, 4),
      p_fdr   = round(p_fdr,   4)
    )
  tbl |>
    mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
      color = if_else(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
    kable(escape = FALSE,
          col.names = italicize_stats(c("Term", "b", "SE", "t", "df", "p (raw)", "p (FDR)")),
          caption = paste0(display_name, ": quadratic time-trend model fixed effects")) |>
    apa_table(full_width = FALSE) |>
    print()
  cat_re_note(res$quadratic)
})
```

## Fixed Effects: Linear-Only Models {.tabset}

```{r lin-fixed-effects, results='asis'}
# Same format/FDR convention as the quadratic fixed-effects tables above,
# but for each biomarker's linear-only model (res$linear), FDR-corrected
# within term x group (immune/hormones), independently of the quadratic
# models' FDR correction above.
all_fixed_effects_lin <- imap_dfr(mlm_list, function(res, name) {

}) |>

  )) |>
  group_by(term, group) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr")) |>
  ungroup()

iwalk(mlm_list, function(res, name) {
  display_name <- recode(name, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α")  # see quad-fixed-effects above
  cat("\n\n### ", display_name, "\n\n")
  tbl <- all_fixed_effects_lin |>
    filter(biomarker == name) |>
    select(term, estimate, std.error, statistic, df, p.value, p_fdr) |>
    mutate(
      across(c(estimate, std.error, statistic, df), \(x) round(x, 3)),
      p.value = round(p.value, 4),
      p_fdr   = round(p_fdr,   4)
    )
  tbl |>
    mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
      color = if_else(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
    kable(escape = FALSE,
          col.names = italicize_stats(c("Term", "b", "SE", "t", "df", "p (raw)", "p (FDR)")),
          caption = paste0(display_name, ": linear-only time-trend model fixed effects")) |>
    apa_table(full_width = FALSE) |>
    print()
  cat_re_note(res$linear, full_structure = "1 + Time | SampleID")
  if (re_structure(res$linear) != re_structure(res$lrt_linear)) {
    cat("\n\nThe model comparison above uses a linear model with a random intercept and linear slope, so that it shares random effects with the quadratic model.\n\n")
  }
})
```

## Biomarker Trajectories (Figure 4)

```{r fig4-trajectories, fig.width=7.09, fig.height=5.1, fig.alt="Seven panels of salivary biomarker trajectories across T1 to T4, showing observed means, model curves with confidence bands, and individual participant lines."}
# Model plotted per biomarker. Change a value here to plot the other model.
fig4_model <- c(
  CRP = "Linear", `IL-10` = "Quadratic", `IL-6` = "Quadratic", `TNF-alpha` = "Quadratic",
  DHEA = "Quadratic", Testosterone = "Quadratic", Cortisol = "Quadratic"
)
micro_sign <- {x <- intToUtf8(956); Encoding(x) <- "UTF-8"; x}

fig4_spec <- tribble(
  ~key,          ~display,        ~unit,                         ~outcome,           ~panel,
  "CRP",         "CRP",           "ng/mL",                       "CRP_log",          "sos_crp_panel",
  "IL-10",       "IL-10",         "pg/mL",                       "IL10_log",         "sos_cytokines_panel",
  "IL-6",        "IL-6",          "pg/mL",                       "IL6_log",          "sos_cytokines_panel",
  "TNF-alpha",   tnf_alpha_label, "pg/mL",                       "TNFalpha_log",     "sos_cytokines_panel",
  "DHEA",        "DHEA",          "pg/mL",                       "DHEA_log",         "sos_hormones_panel",
  "Testosterone","Testosterone",  "pg/mL",                       "Testosterone_log", "sos_hormones_panel",
  "Cortisol",    "Cortisol",      paste0(micro_sign, "g/dL"),    "Cortisol_log",     "sos_hormones_panel"
) |>
  mutate(title = paste0(display, " (", unit, ", ln)"))

fig4_long <- pmap_dfr(fig4_spec, function(key, display, unit, outcome, panel, title) {
  get(panel) |>
    select(SampleID, Time, value = all_of(outcome)) |>
    filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    mutate(key = key, display = display, title = title)
})
check_sample_scope(fig4_long, "fig4_long")

fig4_obs <- fig4_long |>
  group_by(key, display, title, Time) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    mean = mean(value),
    half = qt(.975, n() - 1) * sd(value) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Population-level curve on a fine grid. model.matrix() on the fitted terms
# reuses the model's orthogonal polynomial basis, so X %*% fixef(fit) matches
# predict(re.form = NA); the stopifnot() confirms it. The band is a Wald 95%
# band from the fixed-effects variance-covariance matrix.
fig4_curve <- pmap_dfr(fig4_spec, function(key, display, unit, outcome, panel, title) {
  fit  <- if (fig4_model[[key]] == "Quadratic") mlm_list[[key]]$quadratic else mlm_list[[key]]$linear
  grid <- data.frame(Time = seq(1, 4, length.out = 121))
  fixed_terms <- delete.response(terms(fit, fixed.only = TRUE))
  X    <- model.matrix(fixed_terms, model.frame(fixed_terms, grid))
  pred <- predict(fit, newdata = grid, re.form = NA)
  stopifnot(max(abs(drop(X %*% fixef(fit)) - pred)) < 1e-8)
  se   <- sqrt(diag(X %*% as.matrix(vcov(fit)) %*% t(X)))
  tibble(key = key, display = display, title = title, Time = grid$Time,
         fit = unname(pred), lower = fit - 1.96 * se, upper = fit + 1.96 * se)
})

fig4_annot <- pmap_dfr(fig4_spec, function(key, display, unit, outcome, panel, title) {
  quad <- fig4_model[[key]] == "Quadratic"
  term_row <- if (quad) {
    all_fixed_effects |> filter(biomarker == key, term == "poly(Time, 2)2")
  } else {
    all_fixed_effects_lin |> filter(biomarker == key, term == "Time")
  }
  # b is quoted to keep trailing zeros; the leading minus stays outside the quotes
  # so plotmath draws it as a proper minus sign.
  b_expr <- paste0(if (term_row$estimate < 0) "-" else "",
                   '"', sprintf("%.2f", abs(term_row$estimate)), '"')
  tibble(key = key, display = display, title = title,
         model_label = paste0(fig4_model[[key]], " model, ", if (quad) "quadratic" else "time", " term"),
         stat_label  = paste0("list(italic(b)==", b_expr, ", ", fmt_p_fdr_plain(term_row$p_fdr), ")"))
})

# Headroom so the annotation sits above the data in each free-scale panel.
fig4_top <- fig4_long |>
  group_by(key, display, title) |>
  summarise(top = max(value), span = max(value) - min(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Time = 1, value = top + 0.24 * span)
fig4_annot <- left_join(fig4_annot, fig4_top |> select(key, y = value, span), by = "key") |>
  mutate(y_stat = y - 0.085 * span)

title_order <- fig4_spec$title
fig4_levels <- function(df) mutate(df, title = factor(title, levels = title_order))

fig4_plot <- ggplot(fig4_levels(fig4_long), aes(Time, value)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = SampleID), colour = "grey55", alpha = 0.16, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_blank(data = fig4_levels(fig4_top)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = fig4_levels(fig4_curve), aes(y = fit, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = display),
              alpha = 0.3, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(data = fig4_levels(fig4_curve), aes(y = fit, colour = display), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(data = fig4_levels(fig4_obs), aes(y = mean, ymin = mean - half, ymax = mean + half),
                width = 0.14, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "black") +
  geom_point(data = fig4_levels(fig4_obs), aes(y = mean), size = 1.3, colour = "black") +
  geom_text(data = fig4_levels(fig4_annot), aes(x = 0.85, y = y, label = model_label),
            hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 2, colour = "grey15") +
  geom_text(data = fig4_levels(fig4_annot), aes(x = 0.85, y = y_stat, label = stat_label),
            hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 2, colour = "grey15", parse = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ title, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = biomarker_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = biomarker_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4, limits = c(0.85, 4.15),
                     labels = c("T1\nbaseline", "T2\n~10 min", "T3\n~30 min", "T4\n~60 min")) +
  labs(x = "Time point (minutes after task onset)", y = "ln concentration") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 7.5) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 7.5, hjust = 0),
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey40"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.25, colour = "grey40"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "grey20", size = 6.2),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(3, "mm"),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(3.5, "mm")
  )

dir.create(file.path(proj_path, "figures"), showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave(file.path(proj_path, "figures", "fig4_biomarker_trajectories.png"), fig4_plot,
       device = ragg::agg_png, width = 180, height = 130, units = "mm", dpi = 600, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(proj_path, "figures", "fig4_biomarker_trajectories.pdf"), fig4_plot,
       device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, width = 180, height = 130, units = "mm", bg = "white")

fig4_plot

fig4_quad_names <- fig4_spec$display[fig4_model[fig4_spec$key] == "Quadratic"]
fig4_lin_names  <- fig4_spec$display[fig4_model[fig4_spec$key] == "Linear"]
fig4_n_text <- fig4_obs |>
  mutate(display = factor(display, levels = fig4_spec$display)) |>
  arrange(display, Time) |>
  group_by(display) |>
  summarise(txt = paste0(first(as.character(display)), " ", paste(n, collapse = ", ")), .groups = "drop") |>
  pull(txt) |>
  paste(collapse = "; ")
```

**Figure 4.** Salivary biomarker trajectories across the session (N = 72 analytic sample). Black points are observed mean ln concentrations at each time point, and error bars are their 95% confidence intervals. Coloured curves are population-level fixed-effects predictions (random effects set to zero) from the REML mixed models in the Aim 1c section above, and shaded bands are 95% confidence bands from the fixed-effects variance-covariance matrix. Faint grey lines are individual participants' observed trajectories. Panels show a quadratic model for `r paste(fig4_quad_names, collapse = ", ")` and a linear model for `r paste(fig4_lin_names, collapse = ", ")`. Panel annotations give the model, the coefficient for its highest-order time term (*b*; orthogonal polynomial scale for quadratic models, per time point for linear models), and its FDR-corrected *p*. Each panel has its own y-axis. T2 to T4 are approximate times after task onset. n per time point (T1, T2, T3, T4): `r fig4_n_text`.

```{r ind-growth-curves, fig.width=12, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Individual growth curves by biomarker: observed trajectories, model-fitted individual curves, and population-average quadratic trend"}
panel_map <- list(
  "CRP"          = list(data = sos_crp_panel,       col = "CRP_log"),
  "IL-10"        = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "IL10_log"),
  "IL-6"         = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "IL6_log"),
  "TNF-alpha"    = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "TNFalpha_log"),
  "DHEA"         = list(data = sos_hormones_panel,  col = "DHEA_log"),

)

ind_curve_data <- imap_dfr(mlm_list, function(res, name) {
  pm      <- panel_map[[name]]
  obs_dat <- pm$data |>
    select(SampleID, Time, value = all_of(pm$col)) |>
    filter(!is.na(value))

  obs_dat |>
    mutate(
      fitted_ind = predict(res$quadratic, newdata = obs_dat),
      fitted_pop = predict(res$quadratic, newdata = obs_dat, re.form = NA),
      biomarker    = name
    )
}) |>
  mutate(
    biomarker = recode(biomarker, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α"),
    biomarker = factor(biomarker,
      levels = c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", "TNF-α", "DHEA", "Testosterone", "Cortisol"))
  )

pop_curve <- ind_curve_data |>
  group_by(biomarker, Time) |>
  summarise(fitted_pop = mean(fitted_pop, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Aim 1c (continued): Biomarker Reactivity (Peak vs. Baseline)

*Aim 1c (manuscript): peak (T3 or T4, whichever higher) compared to T1 via two-tailed paired t-tests, FDR-corrected separately within immune markers (4 tests) and hormones (3 tests); reactivity = peak − T1 (see Supplementary Section S3 for a full-trajectory AUCi sensitivity check).*

Each person's peak is the higher of T3 or T4. Reactivity score = peak − T1 (positive = increase from baseline).

## Peak vs. T1 t-tests

```{r peak-ttests}
peak_ttest_tbl <- peak_tests_raw |>
  map(broom::tidy) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "biomarker") |>
  mutate(biomarker = case_match(
    biomarker,
    "crp" ~ "CRP", "il10" ~ "IL-10", "il6" ~ "IL-6", "tnfa" ~ "TNF-α",
    "dhea" ~ "DHEA", "test" ~ "Testosterone", "cort" ~ "Cortisol"
  )) |>
  select(biomarker, estimate, statistic, parameter, p.value) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))

peak_ttest_tbl |>
  mutate(p.value = cell_spec(p.value, bold = p.value < 0.05,
    color = if_else(p.value < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "Mean diff (peak − T1)", "t", "df", "p (two-tailed)")), escape = FALSE,
        caption = "Paired t-tests: biomarker reactivity (peak vs. T1)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

## FDR Correction

```{r fdr}
fdr_tbl <- tibble(
  group   = c(rep("Immune", 4), rep("Hormones", 3)),
  biomarker = c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", "TNF-α", "DHEA", "Testosterone", "Cortisol"),
  p_raw   = round(peak_praw, 6),
  p_fdr   = peak_pfdr
)

fdr_tbl |>
  mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(round(p_fdr, 4), bold = p_fdr < 0.05,
    color = if_else(p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(col.names = italicize_stats(c("Group", "Biomarker", "p (raw)", "p (FDR)")), escape = FALSE,
        caption = "FDR correction: biomarker reactivity (peak vs. T1), within immune and hormone families") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r reactivity-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
sig_immune  <- fdr_tbl |> filter(group == "Immune",   p_fdr < 0.05) |> pull(biomarker)
sig_hormone <- fdr_tbl |> filter(group == "Hormones", p_fdr < 0.05) |> pull(biomarker)
ns_immune   <- fdr_tbl |> filter(group == "Immune",   p_fdr >= 0.05) |> pull(biomarker)
ns_hormone  <- fdr_tbl |> filter(group == "Hormones", p_fdr >= 0.05) |> pull(biomarker)

fmt_sig <- function(x) if (length(x) == 0) "none" else paste(x, collapse = ", ")

react_means <- biomarkers_difference |>
  summarise(across(-SampleID, \(x) round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 3)))
react_sds <- biomarkers_difference |>
  summarise(across(-SampleID, \(x) round(sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), 3)))

peak_tbl_lookup <- peak_ttest_tbl
get_peak <- function(biomarker_name, col) {
  peak_tbl_lookup[peak_tbl_lookup$biomarker == biomarker_name, col]
}
```

**Results.** Biomarker reactivity was operationalized as the difference between each participant's peak sample (T3 or T4) and baseline (T1). After FDR correction within immune markers and hormones separately, significant baseline-to-peak increases were observed for the following immune markers: `r fmt_sig(sig_immune)`; and for the following hormones: `r fmt_sig(sig_hormone)`. `r if (length(ns_immune) > 0) paste0(paste(ns_immune, collapse=", "), " did not show significant immune reactivity after FDR correction.")` `r if (length(ns_hormone) > 0) paste0(paste(ns_hormone, collapse=", "), " did not show significant hormonal reactivity after FDR correction.")`

## T3 vs. T4: Which Timepoint Captured the Peak?

*Restricting attention to T3 and T4 only (T2 is excluded here — it may reflect scan-environment
arousal or TiM task recording rather than the SOS task itself): for each biomarker, how many participants' peak
(the higher of T3/T4) fell at T3 vs. T4 — both overall, and restricted to participants who
showed an actual increase over T1 ("responders").*

```{r t3-vs-t4-counts, echo=FALSE}
count_t3_vs_t4 <- function(data, t3_col, t4_col, t1_col) {
  dat <- data |> select(all_of(c(t3_col, t4_col, t1_col))) |> na.omit()
  peak <- pmax(dat[[t3_col]], dat[[t4_col]])
  resp <- peak > dat[[t1_col]]
  tibble(
    n_valid          = nrow(dat),
    n_peaked_T3      = sum(dat[[t3_col]] > dat[[t4_col]]),
    n_peaked_T4      = sum(dat[[t4_col]] > dat[[t3_col]]),
    n_tie            = sum(dat[[t3_col]] == dat[[t4_col]]),
    n_responders     = sum(resp),
    n_resp_peaked_T3 = sum(dat[[t3_col]] > dat[[t4_col]] & resp),
    n_resp_peaked_T4 = sum(dat[[t4_col]] > dat[[t3_col]] & resp)
  )
}

t3_vs_t4_specs <- list(
  CRP          = list(d = sos_crp_wide,       t3 = "CRP_log_3",          t4 = "CRP_log_4",          t1 = "CRP_log_1"),
  `IL-10`      = list(d = sos_cytokines_wide, t3 = "IL10_log_3",         t4 = "IL10_log_4",         t1 = "IL10_log_1"),
  `IL-6`       = list(d = sos_cytokines_wide, t3 = "IL6_log_3",          t4 = "IL6_log_4",          t1 = "IL6_log_1"),
  `TNF-α`      = list(d = sos_cytokines_wide, t3 = "TNFalpha_log_3",     t4 = "TNFalpha_log_4",     t1 = "TNFalpha_log_1"),
  DHEA         = list(d = sos_hormones_wide,  t3 = "DHEA_log_3",         t4 = "DHEA_log_4",         t1 = "DHEA_log_1"),
  Testosterone = list(d = sos_hormones_wide,  t3 = "Testosterone_log_3", t4 = "Testosterone_log_4", t1 = "Testosterone_log_1"),
  Cortisol     = list(d = sos_hormones_wide,  t3 = "Cortisol_log_3",     t4 = "Cortisol_log_4",     t1 = "Cortisol_log_1")
)

t3_vs_t4_tbl <- imap_dfr(t3_vs_t4_specs, function(s, name) {
  count_t3_vs_t4(s$d, s$t3, s$t4, s$t1) |> mutate(biomarker = name, .before = 1)
})
```

```{r t3-vs-t4-table-all}
t3_vs_t4_tbl |>
  select(biomarker, n_valid, n_peaked_T3, n_peaked_T4, n_tie) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "N (valid T3 & T4)", "Peaked at T3", "Peaked at T4", "Tied")),
        caption = "Which timepoint (T3 or T4) had the higher value, all participants") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r t3-vs-t4-table-responders}
t3_vs_t4_tbl |>
  select(biomarker, n_responders, n_resp_peaked_T3, n_resp_peaked_T4) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "N responders (peak > T1)", "...peaked at T3", "...peaked at T4")),
        caption = "Among responders only: which timepoint (T3 or T4) captured the peak") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r t3-vs-t4-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
t3_lean_df <- t3_vs_t4_tbl |> filter(n_resp_peaked_T3 > n_resp_peaked_T4)
t4_lean_df <- t3_vs_t4_tbl |> filter(n_resp_peaked_T4 > n_resp_peaked_T3)
t3_lean <- if (nrow(t3_lean_df) == 0) "none" else paste(t3_lean_df$biomarker, collapse = ", ")
t4_lean <- if (nrow(t4_lean_df) == 0) "none" else paste(t4_lean_df$biomarker, collapse = ", ")
```

**Results.** Among responders (participants whose peak — the higher of T3 or T4 — exceeded
their own T1 baseline), the following biomarkers leaned toward peaking at T3 rather than T4:
`r t3_lean`. The following leaned toward peaking at T4 rather than T3: `r t4_lean`.

## Sensitivity Analysis: AUCi

The AUCi-based sensitivity analysis (one-sample tests of area-under-the-curve-with-respect-to-increase
reactivity, plus the diurnal-rhythm check of steroid hormone AUCi against time since waking and session
start time) has moved to `sos-bioreactivity-supplement.qmd`, Sections S3 (AUCi-Based Reactivity) and S4
(Diurnal Rhythm Check), alongside the other sensitivity analyses now consolidated there. See Supplementary
Sections S3–S4 for the full one-sample AUCi tests, the peak-vs-AUCi head-to-head tables for Aim 2
(pubertal status/timing) and Aim 3 (BFNES, CES-DC), and the diurnal-rhythm correlation check.

# Aim 1d: Correlations Among Reactivity Measures

*Aim 1d (manuscript): bivariate Pearson correlations among all magnitude-of-change (reactivity) difference scores.*

```{r corr-matrix, fig.width=10, fig.height=9, fig.cap="Correlation matrix: all 13 reactivity outcomes (* = FDR-corrected p < .05 within domain)"}
diff_matrix <- all_difference |> select(-SampleID) |> as.matrix()
colnames(diff_matrix) <- c(
  "ΔHR: Task vs. Rest", "ΔHR: Both Watch You vs. You Watch You", "ΔHR: Both Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer", "ΔHR: Both Watch You vs. Fixation-Cross",
  "ΔCRP", "ΔIL-10", "ΔIL-6", "ΔTNF-α", "ΔDHEA", "ΔTestosterone", "ΔCortisol",
  "ΔSubj Stress: Both Watch You vs. You Watch You", "ΔSubj Stress: Both Watch You vs. Both Watch Peer"
)
difference_rcorrs <- rcorr(diff_matrix)

plot_sig_corrplot <- function(r_mat, p_mat, title = "", type = "upper",
                              cl.ratio = 0.15, cl.cex = 1.15,
                              tl.cex = 1.0, mar = NULL, diag = FALSE) {
  if (is.null(mar)) {
    mar <- c(0, 0, if (nchar(title) > 0) 2 else 0, 0)
  }
  corrplot(
    r_mat,
    p.mat     = p_mat,
    sig.level = 0.05,
    # Mark significant cells with * rather than crossing out the rest, so every
    # correlation stays readable. p_mat decides which p (FDR or raw); the
    # figure caption says which.
    # corrplot's label_sig errors when no cell is significant, so skip it then.
    insig     = if (any(p_mat < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)) "label_sig" else "n",
    pch.col   = "black",
    pch.cex   = 1.6,
    method    = "circle",
    type      = type,
    tl.col    = "black",
    tl.srt    = 90,  # vertical: long condition labels overflow the right edge at 45
    tl.cex    = tl.cex,
    col       = colorRampPalette(c("#d73027", "white", "#4575b4"))(200),
    diag      = diag,
    title     = title,
    mar       = mar,
    cl.ratio  = cl.ratio,
    cl.cex    = cl.cex
  )
}

diff_domains <- list(
  hr      = 1:4,
  immune  = 5:8,
  hormone = 9:11,
  subj    = 12:13
)

fdr_diff_mat <- difference_rcorrs$P
for (idx in diff_domains) {
  sub <- fdr_diff_mat[idx, idx, drop = FALSE]
  ut  <- upper.tri(sub)
  sub[ut] <- p.adjust(sub[ut], method = "fdr")
  sub[lower.tri(sub)] <- t(sub)[lower.tri(sub)]
  fdr_diff_mat[idx, idx] <- sub
}

plot_sig_corrplot(difference_rcorrs$r, fdr_diff_mat)
```

*Circle size and color reflect correlation magnitude (red = negative, blue = positive). \* marks correlations significant after FDR correction (p~FDR~ < .05). FDR applied within domain (HR, immune markers, hormones, subjective stress); cross-domain pairs shown at raw p.*

## Correlation p-values

```{r corr-pvalues}
# fdr_diff_mat already computed in corr-matrix chunk above
fdr_diff_mat |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) {
    sig  <- !is.na(x) & x < 0.05
    xlab <- if_else(is.na(x), "—", as.character(round(x, 4)))
    cell_spec(xlab, bold = sig, color = if_else(sig, "#2166ac", "black"))
  })) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        caption = "P-values FDR-corrected within domain (HR, immune, hormones, subjective stress); cross-domain pairs raw (bold = p < .05).") |>
  apa_table()
```

## Correlation r-values

```{r corr-rvalues}
# Same matrix as the corrplot above and the p-value table below -- no numeric
# r-value table previously existed for this 13x13 matrix (unlike the
# equivalent puberty/timing correlation sections further down, which do have
# one); adding it here so every r can be read directly rather than only
# estimated from the corrplot circle size/color.
r_diff_mat <- difference_rcorrs$r
sig_diff_mat <- fdr_diff_mat < 0.05

r_diff_df <- as.data.frame(
  matrix(
    mapply(function(r, sig) {
      cell_spec(round(r, 3), bold = !is.na(sig) & sig,
                color = if_else(!is.na(sig) & sig, "#2166ac", "black"))
    }, r_diff_mat, sig_diff_mat),
    nrow = nrow(r_diff_mat), ncol = ncol(r_diff_mat),
    dimnames = dimnames(r_diff_mat)
  )
)

r_diff_df |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        caption = "Pearson r among the 13 reactivity difference scores (bold = significant per the FDR/raw convention in the p-value table above).") |>
  apa_table()
```

## Correlation Sample Sizes: Subjective Stress Rows

```{r corr-n-subj}
# Pairwise-complete n (from rcorr()) for the two subjective-stress difference
# scores against every other reactivity outcome, including each other --
# printed explicitly since n varies pair-to-pair (not every participant has
# every outcome) and isn't otherwise visible in the r/p matrices above.
n_diff_mat <- difference_rcorrs$n

n_diff_mat[diff_domains$subj, , drop = FALSE] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  kable(caption = "Pairwise-complete n: ΔSubj Stress rows against all 13 reactivity outcomes") |>
  apa_table()
```

```{r corr-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
p_upper <- fdr_diff_mat
p_upper[lower.tri(p_upper, diag = TRUE)] <- NA
r_upper <- difference_rcorrs$r
r_upper[lower.tri(r_upper, diag = TRUE)] <- NA

n_corr_pairs_total <- sum(!is.na(p_upper))
n_corr_sig         <- sum(p_upper < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# Largest positive and negative r among sig pairs
sig_r_vals <- r_upper[!is.na(p_upper) & p_upper < 0.05]
corr_r_range <- if (length(sig_r_vals) > 0) {
  paste0("ranging from r = ", round(min(sig_r_vals), 2), " to r = ", round(max(sig_r_vals), 2))
} else {
  ""
}
```

**Results.** Bivariate Pearson correlations among the 13 reactivity difference scores are shown in the matrix above (full p-value table below). P-values were FDR-corrected within domain (among the four HR reactivity measures, among immune markers, among hormones, and among subjective stress ratings); cross-domain pairs are reported at raw p. Of `r n_corr_pairs_total` unique pairs, `r n_corr_sig` were statistically significant (`r corr_r_range`). Within-domain associations tended to be positive, reflecting coherence within each response system. Cross-domain associations between physiological and subjective reactivity are reported in context throughout the sections below.
