# Aim 2 (Exploratory): Pubertal Maturation and Reactivity

*Aim 2 (manuscript, exploratory): bivariate Pearson correlations between each of the 13 reactivity outcomes and pubertal status (PDS score average), and three operationalizations of pubertal timing: (1) status-for-age (effect of pubertal status while controlling for age), (2) perceived pubertal timing reported from the PDS and (3) age at menarche.*

Pubertal maturation is examined here as a developmental moderator of reactivity to the SOS task, per the manuscript's current framing — an exploratory aim, not a primary hypothesis test.

Note: pubertal status is tested here using the PUBcomp composite (PDS+line drawings composite), computed in `pubcomp-SOS.R` from `data/SOS-pubcomp.csv`. Age at menarche and self-reported perceived timing (PDS F5) still come from the raw PDS questionnaire, since those items are not carried forward into `SOS-pubcomp.csv`. Both puberty and age are centered in the first timing operationalization.

```{r puberty-load, echo=FALSE}
# dob_session_raw and age_df (age at session, for computing pubertal timing
# residuals) were already loaded in the Sample Descriptives > Age chunk above.

# Pubertal status: PUBcomp (PDS+line drawings composite), computed in pubcomp-SOS.R
# from data/SOS-pubcomp.csv
sos_puberty <- read.csv(here::here("data", "SOS-pubcomp.csv")) |>
  select(SampleID = SID, PUBcomp) |>
  filter(SampleID %in% biomarker_ids)
check_sample_scope(sos_puberty, "sos_puberty")

# PDS F5 (perceived timing) and menarche date are not carried forward into
# SOS-pubcomp.csv, so they're still read from the raw PDS questionnaire
pds_full_raw <- read.csv(file.path(
  data_path, "SOS/SOS-study-monash/questionnaires/CESD_PDS.csv"
))

pds_f5_df <- pds_full_raw |>
  select(SampleID, PDS_F5) |>
  mutate(PDS_F5 = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(PDS_F5)))

timing_base <- sos_puberty |>
  left_join(age_df, by = "SampleID") |>
  filter(!is.na(age_at_session))

# Age at menarche: parse PDS_F9 (free-text date of first period) + DOB → age in years
pds_raw <- pds_full_raw |>
  select(SampleID, menarche_date_raw = PDS_F9)

parse_menarche_date <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  x <- gsub("(\\d+)(st|nd|rd|th)", "\\1", x, ignore.case = TRUE)  # strip ordinals
  suppressWarnings(lubridate::parse_date_time(
    x,
    orders = c("mdy", "mdY", "BdY", "bdY",
               "YBd", "Ybd", "BY", "bY", "by",   # "by" catches "Sep-17"
               "Y", "dBY", "dbY"),
    quiet  = TRUE
  ))
}

dob_df <- dob_session_raw |>
  filter(redcap_event_name == "ongoing_records_arm_1") |>
  select(SampleID, dob) |>
  mutate(dob = as.Date(lubridate::parse_date_time(dob, orders = c("ymd", "mdy"))))

# Hand-coded menarche dates for free-text PDS_F9 answers the parser can't read
# but that give enough to estimate a date. Unknown day -> 15th; relative answers
# are anchored to the SOS session date. Not recoverable: TAG059 ("not sure"),
# TAG141 ("I forgot"), TAG176 ("right before 7th grade" -- too imprecise).
menarche_manual <- tribble(
  ~SampleID, ~menarche_date_manual, ~raw_answer,
  "TAG048", as.Date("2014-09-16"), "september of 2014? probably around the 16th",
  "TAG084", as.Date("2014-03-15"), "3/?/14",
  "TAG309", as.Date("2017-10-20"), "~2 years ago (session 2019-10-20)",
  "TAG312", as.Date("2019-09-15"), "sometime last month this year (session 2019-10-26)"
)

menarche_df <- pds_raw |>
  left_join(dob_df, by = "SampleID") |>
  left_join(menarche_manual |> select(-raw_answer), by = "SampleID") |>
  mutate(
    menarche_date = as.Date(parse_menarche_date(menarche_date_raw)),
    menarche_date = coalesce(menarche_date, menarche_date_manual),
    age_menarche  = as.numeric(menarche_date - dob) / 365.25
  ) |>
  select(SampleID, age_menarche)

timing_df <- timing_base |>
  left_join(menarche_df, by = "SampleID") |>
  left_join(pds_f5_df, by = "SampleID") |>
  mutate(
    PUBcomp_c         = PUBcomp         - mean(PUBcomp,         na.rm = TRUE),
    age_at_session_c  = age_at_session  - mean(age_at_session,  na.rm = TRUE),
    age_menarche_c    = age_menarche    - mean(age_menarche,    na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  select(SampleID, age_at_session, age_at_session_c,
         PUBcomp, PUBcomp_c, age_menarche, age_menarche_c, PDS_F5)
```

```{r puberty-processing, echo=FALSE}

  )

# puberty_vars = pubertal status measure from SOS-pubcomp.csv; puberty_labels

puberty_label_map <- c(PUBcomp = "Pubertal Status (Composite)")

# Timing variables (defined here so they are available for the combined matrix below)
timing_vars   <- c("age_menarche_c", "PDS_F5")
timing_labels <- c("Age at menarche (centered, years)",
                   "PDS F5: perceived timing (1=much earlier, 5=much later)")
timing_reactivity  <- all_difference |>

reactivity_vars <- c(
  "task_rs_hr_diff", "conn_dis_hr_diff", "conn_other_hr_diff", "conn_rest_hr_diff",
  "crp_difference", "il10_difference", "il6_difference", "tnfa_difference",

)

reactivity_labels <- c(
```

## Correlations: All Puberty Variables × Reactivity

Rows include pubertal status (PDS+line drawings composite), age at menarche, and PDS F5 perceived timing; columns are all reactivity outcomes.

```{r all-puberty-corr-matrix, fig.width=14, fig.height=7.5, fig.cap="Correlation matrix: pubertal status/timing variables x all 13 reactivity outcomes (* = FDR-corrected p < .05 within domain)"}
all_pub_vars   <- c(puberty_vars, timing_vars)
all_pub_labels <- c(puberty_labels, timing_labels)

all_pub_mat <- timing_reactivity |>
  select(all_of(c(all_pub_vars, reactivity_vars))) |>
  as.matrix()
colnames(all_pub_mat) <- c(all_pub_labels, reactivity_labels)

all_pub_corrs   <- rcorr(all_pub_mat)
pub_react_corrs <- all_pub_corrs   # alias for downstream inline text

# FDR computed HERE so corrplot and table use identical p-values.
# Each puberty/timing variable is its own family, corrected separately within
# each reactivity domain (e.g. PUBcomp x HR is one family, PUBcomp x hormones
# is a separate family, age at menarche x HR is yet another separate family).
hr_cols   <- reactivity_labels[1:4]
imm_cols  <- reactivity_labels[5:8]
horm_cols <- reactivity_labels[9:11]
subj_cols <- reactivity_labels[12:13]

raw_allpub_mat <- all_pub_corrs$P[all_pub_labels, reactivity_labels, drop = FALSE]
fdr_allpub_mat <- raw_allpub_mat
for (pv in all_pub_labels) {
  for (cols in list(hr_cols, imm_cols, horm_cols, subj_cols)) {
    fdr_allpub_mat[pv, cols] <- p.adjust(raw_allpub_mat[pv, cols], method = "fdr")
  }
}

# * marks reflect FDR-corrected significance (matches the table below)
plot_sig_corrplot(
  all_pub_corrs$r[all_pub_labels, reactivity_labels, drop = FALSE],
  fdr_allpub_mat,
  type = "full", cl.ratio = 0.06, cl.cex = 1.1,
  tl.cex = 0.95, mar = c(0, 0, 1, 6), diag = TRUE
)
```

*\* marks correlations significant after FDR correction (p~FDR~ < .05). FDR applied separately for each puberty/timing variable, within each reactivity domain.*

```{r all-puberty-corr-pvalues}
fdr_allpub_mat |>

    sig  <- !is.na(x) & x < 0.05
    xlab <- if_else(is.na(x), "—", as.character(round(x, 4)))
    cell_spec(xlab, bold = sig, color = if_else(sig, "#2166ac", "black"))
  })) |>
```

```{r all-puberty-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
sig_allpub <- expand.grid(pv = all_pub_labels, rv = reactivity_labels,
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    r     = round(r_mat[pv, rv], 3),
    p_fdr = round(fdr_allpub_mat[pv, rv], 4),
    sig   = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
    label = paste0(pv, " × ", rv, " (r = ", r, ", p~FDR~ = ", p_fdr, ")")
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(sig)

n_allpub_pairs_total <- length(all_pub_labels) * length(reactivity_labels)
n_sig_allpub          <- nrow(sig_allpub)
sig_allpub_text       <- if (n_sig_allpub == 0) "none survived FDR correction" else
  paste(sig_allpub$label, collapse = "; ")

# Describe direction only when every significant pair shares one sign and outcome,
# so the prose stays accurate if the underlying data/results change on re-render.
allpub_dir_text <- ""
if (n_sig_allpub > 0) {
  same_outcome <- n_distinct(sig_allpub$rv) == 1
  same_sign    <- n_distinct(sign(sig_allpub$r)) == 1
  if (same_outcome && same_sign) {
    dir_word <- if (unique(sign(sig_allpub$r)) > 0) "greater" else "smaller"
    allpub_dir_text <- paste0(
      " All significant associations involved ", unique(sig_allpub$rv),
      ", such that higher values on these puberty/timing variables were associated with ",
      dir_word, " reactivity on this outcome."
    )
  }
}
```

**Results.** Across the `r n_allpub_pairs_total` puberty/timing-variable × reactivity-outcome pairs tested (pubertal status — PDS+line drawings composite — plus age at menarche and PDS F5 perceived timing, each against all 13 reactivity outcomes; FDR-corrected within each reactivity domain), `r n_sig_allpub` association`r if (n_sig_allpub != 1) "s" else ""` remained significant after correction: `r sig_allpub_text`.`r allpub_dir_text` No other puberty or timing variable was significantly associated with reactivity after FDR correction.

## Puberty Status as Predictor of Reactivity

Simple regressions: reactivity ~ pubertal status (mean-centered).

```{r puberty-regressions, results='asis'}
pv_c <- paste0(puberty_vars, "_c")   # centered counterparts

for (i in seq_along(puberty_vars)) {
  pv  <- puberty_vars[i]
  pvc <- pv_c[i]
  cat("\n\n###", puberty_labels[i], "(centered)\n\n")
  reg_tbl <- map_dfr(setNames(reactivity_vars, reactivity_labels), function(rv) {
    dat <- puberty_reactivity |> select(all_of(c(rv, pvc))) |> na.omit()
    if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
    fit <- lm(as.formula(paste(rv, "~", pvc)), data = dat)
    broom::tidy(fit) |>
      filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
      mutate(term = pv, outcome = rv, .before = 1)
  }, .id = "Reactivity") |>
    select(Reactivity, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) |>
    mutate(p_fdr = round(p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
    mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, statistic), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
    mutate(p.value = round(p.value, 4))

  reg_tbl |>
    mutate(
      p.value = as.character(p.value),
      p_fdr   = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
        color = if_else(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))
    ) |>
    kable(escape = FALSE,
          col.names = italicize_stats(c("Reactivity outcome", "b", "SE", "t", "p (raw)", "p (FDR)")),
          caption = paste0(puberty_labels[i], " (centered): simple regression on each reactivity outcome")) |>
    apa_table(full_width = FALSE) |>
    print()
}
```

# Aim 2 (continued, Exploratory): Pubertal Timing and Reactivity

Pubertal timing is operationalized here as (1) **age at menarche** (lower = earlier onset), (2) perceived pubertal timing as reported on the PDS, and (3) the regression below enters centered pubertal status (PUBcomp) and centered age simultaneously, so each coefficient controls for the other.

```{r timing-processing, echo=FALSE}
# timing_reactivity, timing_vars, timing_labels defined in puberty-processing chunk
```

## Descriptives

```{r timing-descriptives}
timing_df |>
  select(age_at_session, PUBcomp, PDS_F5, age_menarche) |>
  psych::describe() |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(n, mean, sd, min, max, skew, kurtosis) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Variable") |>
  mutate(Variable = recode(Variable,
    age_at_session   = "Age at session (years)",
    PUBcomp          = "Pubertal status (Composite)",
    PDS_F5 = "Perceived Pubertal Timing",
    age_menarche     = "Age at menarche (years)"
  )) |>
  kable(caption = "Pubertal timing descriptives") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

## Correlations: Timing × Reactivity

*See combined puberty correlation matrix above for age-at-menarche and PDS F5 correlations with all reactivity outcomes.*

## Timing as Predictor of Reactivity

Each reactivity outcome is regressed on centered pubertal status (PUBcomp) and centered age (`age_at_session_c`) simultaneously. The status coefficient reflects status beyond what is expected for age (early timing); the `age_at_session_c` coefficient reflects age beyond what is expected for status.

```{r timing-regressions, results='asis'}
timing_joint_tbl <- map_dfr(seq_along(puberty_vars), function(i) {
  pv       <- puberty_vars[i]
  pvc      <- paste0(pv, "_c")
  pv_label <- puberty_labels[i]

  map_dfr(setNames(reactivity_vars, reactivity_labels), function(rv) {
    dat <- timing_reactivity |>
      select(all_of(c(rv, pvc, "age_at_session_c"))) |>
      na.omit()
    if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
    fit <- lm(as.formula(paste(rv, "~", pvc, "+ age_at_session_c")), data = dat)
    broom::tidy(fit) |>
      filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
      mutate(
        term = if_else(term == pvc,
                        paste0(pv_label, " (centered)"),
                        "Age at session (centered)"),
        across(c(estimate, std.error, statistic), \(x) round(x, 3)),
        p.value = round(p.value, 4)
      )
  }, .id = "Reactivity") |>
    mutate(measure = pv_label, .before = 1)
}) |>
  group_by(measure, term) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = round(p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
  ungroup()

for (ms in unique(timing_joint_tbl$measure)) {
  cat("\n\n###", ms, "\n\n")
  for (trm in unique(timing_joint_tbl$term[timing_joint_tbl$measure == ms])) {
    cat("\n\n####", trm, "\n\n")
    timing_joint_tbl |>
      filter(measure == ms, term == trm) |>
      select(Reactivity, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, p_fdr) |>
      mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
        color = if_else(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
      kable(escape = FALSE,
            col.names = italicize_stats(c("Reactivity outcome", "b", "SE", "t", "p (raw)", "p (FDR)")),
            caption = paste("Reactivity ~", trm, "+ other term (both centered); FDR within measure × term")) |>
      apa_table(full_width = FALSE) |>
      print()
  }
}
```

```{r timing-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
fmt_timing_sig <- function(df) {
  if (nrow(df) == 0) return("none reached statistical significance after FDR correction")
  paste(
    paste0(df$Reactivity, " (*b* = ", df$estimate, ", *p*~FDR~ = ", df$p_fdr, ")"),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}

timing_summary <- lapply(puberty_labels, function(pv_label) {
  status_term <- paste0(pv_label, " (centered)")
  sig_status  <- timing_joint_tbl |> filter(measure == pv_label, term == status_term, p_fdr < 0.05)
  sig_age     <- timing_joint_tbl |> filter(measure == pv_label, term == "Age at session (centered)", p_fdr < 0.05)
  list(
    label       = pv_label,
    n_status    = nrow(sig_status), status_text = fmt_timing_sig(sig_status),
    n_age       = nrow(sig_age),    age_text    = fmt_timing_sig(sig_age)
  )
})

timing_results_paragraph <- paste(sapply(timing_summary, function(s) {
  paste0(
    "For ", s$label, ", ", s$n_status,
    " outcome", if (s$n_status != 1) "s" else "", " showed a significant status-beyond-age effect (",
    s$status_text, "), and ", s$n_age,
    " outcome", if (s$n_age != 1) "s" else "", " showed a significant age-beyond-status effect (",
    s$age_text, ")."
  )
}), collapse = " ")
```

**Results.** To disentangle pubertal status from chronological age, each reactivity outcome was regressed simultaneously on mean-centered pubertal status (PDS+line drawings composite) and mean-centered age at session (`age_at_session_c`). The status coefficient reflects status beyond that expected for age (i.e., early maturation); the `age_at_session_c` coefficient reflects age beyond that expected for status. After FDR correction within each predictor term across all 13 reactivity outcomes: `r timing_results_paragraph` Scatter plots of timing predictors against biomarker reactivity outcomes are shown below.

## Forest Plot: Effect of Pubertal Status Controlling for Age

Effect of pubertal status (PUBcomp, centered) on each reactivity outcome, from the joint model above (`reactivity ~ pubertal status + age at session`, both centered). Points are the status coefficient; bars are 95% CI; blue marks FDR-significant effects (*p*~FDR~ < .05).

```{r timing-status-forest, fig.width=10, fig.height=6.5, fig.cap="Forest plot: effect of pubertal status on reactivity, controlling for age"}
# Greek letters (Delta, beta) built via intToUtf8() and re-tagged as UTF-8
# rather than relying on the literal characters already in reactivity_labels
# surviving whatever locale this renders under -- under a "C" locale, R's
# text-rendering path (ggplot/grid) can misread genuinely-correct UTF-8 bytes
# tagged Encoding="unknown" as single-byte junk, even though e.g. a kable/HTML
# table of the same strings displays fine (browser text isn't subject to
# this). Cheap insurance either way.
delta_sym <- intToUtf8(916)
beta_sym  <- intToUtf8(946)
cardio_domain_label <- paste0("Cardiovascular (", delta_sym, "HR)")

status_term_label <- paste0(puberty_labels[1], " (centered)")

forest_dat <- timing_joint_tbl |>
  filter(term == status_term_label) |>
  mutate(Reactivity = {x <- Reactivity; Encoding(x) <- "UTF-8"; x}) |>
  mutate(
    domain = case_when(
      grepl("^.HR:", Reactivity) ~ cardio_domain_label,
      grepl("Subj Stress", Reactivity) ~ "Subjective Stress",
      TRUE ~ "Biomarkers"
    ),
    domain = factor(domain, levels = c(cardio_domain_label, "Biomarkers", "Subjective Stress")),
    sig    = ifelse(p_fdr < 0.05, "FDR-significant (p < .05)", "Not significant"),
    ci_lo  = estimate - 1.96 * std.error,
    ci_hi  = estimate + 1.96 * std.error,
    Reactivity = factor(Reactivity, levels = rev({x <- reactivity_labels; Encoding(x) <- "UTF-8"; x}))
  )

ggplot(forest_dat, aes(x = estimate, y = Reactivity, color = sig)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey45") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi), width = 0, linewidth = 0.7, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(domain), scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FDR-significant (p < .05)" = "#2a78d6", "Not significant" = "#b9b8b2")) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("Effect of pubertal status on reactivity (", beta_sym, ", controlling for age)"),
    y = NULL,
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

## Trend Plot: Age-Adjusted Effect of Pubertal Status on Reactivity

The forest plot above shows the size of the age-adjusted pubertal-status effect; this shows the trend itself. Each panel is a **partial-residual (added-variable) plot**: both pubertal status and the reactivity outcome are first residualized on age at session, then plotted against each other. The slope of the fitted line in each panel is mathematically identical to that outcome's status coefficient in the joint model above -- this is what that coefficient looks like as a scatter of actual data rather than a single point estimate.

```{r timing-status-trend, fig.width=13, fig.height=9, fig.cap="Age-adjusted effect of pubertal status on reactivity: partial-residual plots, all 13 outcomes"}
status_sig <- timing_joint_tbl |>
  filter(term == status_term_label) |>
  select(Reactivity, p_fdr) |>
  mutate(sig = ifelse(p_fdr < 0.05, "FDR-significant (p < .05)", "Not significant"))

react_partial <- map_dfr(setNames(reactivity_vars, reactivity_labels), function(rv) {
  dat <- timing_reactivity |>
    select(all_of(c(rv, "PUBcomp", "age_at_session"))) |>
    na.omit()
  if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
  resid_y <- resid(lm(as.formula(paste(rv, "~ age_at_session")), data = dat))
  resid_x <- resid(lm(PUBcomp ~ age_at_session, data = dat))
  tibble(resid_status = resid_x, resid_outcome = resid_y)
}, .id = "Reactivity") |>
  left_join(status_sig, by = "Reactivity") |>
  mutate(
    domain = case_when(
      grepl("^.HR:", Reactivity) ~ cardio_domain_label,
      grepl("Subj Stress", Reactivity) ~ "Subjective Stress",
      TRUE ~ "Biomarkers"
    ),
    domain = factor(domain, levels = c(cardio_domain_label, "Biomarkers", "Subjective Stress")),
    Reactivity = {x <- Reactivity; Encoding(x) <- "UTF-8"; x},
    Reactivity = factor(Reactivity, levels = {x <- reactivity_labels; Encoding(x) <- "UTF-8"; x})
  )

# Panel titles carry each outcome's units (free y-scales, so one axis title
# can't). Reactivity is peak - T1; for biomarkers that is a difference of ln
# concentrations.
reactivity_with_units <- function(lbl) {
  micro <- {x <- intToUtf8(956); Encoding(x) <- "UTF-8"; x}
  unit <- dplyr::case_when(
    startsWith(lbl, "ΔHR")          ~ "bpm",
    startsWith(lbl, "ΔSubj Stress") ~ "rating points",
    lbl == "ΔCRP"                   ~ "ln ng/mL",
    lbl == "ΔCortisol"              ~ paste0("ln ", micro, "g/dL"),
    TRUE                            ~ "ln pg/mL"
  )
  out <- paste0(stringr::str_wrap(lbl, 26), "\n(", unit, ")")
  Encoding(out) <- "UTF-8"
  out
}

ggplot(react_partial, aes(x = resid_status, y = resid_outcome)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5, color = "grey30") +
  geom_smooth(aes(color = sig, fill = sig), method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~Reactivity, scales = "free", ncol = 4,
             labeller = as_labeller(reactivity_with_units)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FDR-significant (p < .05)" = "#2a78d6", "Not significant" = "#b9b8b2"), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FDR-significant (p < .05)" = "#2a78d6", "Not significant" = "#b9b8b2"), drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Pubertal status (residualized on age)",
    y = "Reactivity, residualized on age (units in panel titles)",
    color = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

### Trend Plot: Significant Relationships Only

Same partial-residual plots as above, restricted to the `r sum(status_sig$sig == "FDR-significant (p < .05)")` outcomes that survived FDR correction -- a cleaner figure for highlighting just the significant status-beyond-age effects.

```{r timing-status-trend-sig, fig.width=8, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Age-adjusted effect of pubertal status on reactivity: partial-residual plots, FDR-significant outcomes only"}
react_partial_sig <- react_partial |> filter(sig == "FDR-significant (p < .05)")

ggplot(react_partial_sig, aes(x = resid_status, y = resid_outcome)) +

  facet_wrap(~Reactivity, scales = "free", ncol = 2,
             labeller = as_labeller(reactivity_with_units)) +

    x = "Pubertal status (residualized on age)",
    y = "Reactivity, residualized on age (units in panel titles)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"))
```

## Correlation Matrix: Pubertal Timing, Age, and Psychosocial Predictors

Intercorrelations among the individual-difference predictors used across the puberty and psychosocial hypotheses: pubertal status (PUBcomp composite), age at menarche, perceived pubertal timing (PDS F5), age at session, BFNES (fear of negative evaluation), and CES-DC (depressive symptoms). This is not a predictor-vs-reactivity matrix (those are reported separately above and in Aim 3 below) -- it's the relationships among the predictors themselves, useful for spotting overlap/multicollinearity before interpreting single-predictor models one at a time.

```{r predictors-corr-matrix, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Correlation matrix: pubertal timing, age, and psychosocial predictors (* = FDR-corrected p < .05)"}
predictors_df <- timing_df |>
  select(SampleID, PUBcomp, age_menarche, PDS_F5, age_at_session) |>
  left_join(bfnes, by = "SampleID") |>
  left_join(dep, by = "SampleID")

predictors_matrix <- predictors_df |> select(-SampleID) |> as.matrix()
colnames(predictors_matrix) <- c(
  "Pubertal Status (Composite)", "Age at Menarche", "Perceived Pubertal Timing (PDS F5)",
  "Age at Session", "BFNES (Fear of Negative Evaluation)", "CES-D (Depression)"
)

predictors_rcorrs <- rcorr(predictors_matrix)

# Single family of 15 pairwise tests (these 6 predictors don't split into the
# domain blocks the reactivity-outcome matrices use), FDR-corrected together.
predictors_fdr_mat <- predictors_rcorrs$P
ut <- upper.tri(predictors_fdr_mat)
predictors_fdr_mat[ut] <- p.adjust(predictors_fdr_mat[ut], method = "fdr")
predictors_fdr_mat[lower.tri(predictors_fdr_mat)] <- t(predictors_fdr_mat)[lower.tri(predictors_fdr_mat)]

plot_sig_corrplot(predictors_rcorrs$r, predictors_fdr_mat)
```

*Circle size and color reflect correlation magnitude (red = negative, blue = positive). \* marks correlations significant after FDR correction (p~FDR~ < .05, applied across all 15 pairs). Sample sizes vary by pair due to missingness -- age at menarche has the fewest valid cases (n = `r sum(!is.na(predictors_matrix[, "Age at Menarche"]))`), while most other variables have n = `r max(colSums(!is.na(predictors_matrix)))`; `rcorr()` uses pairwise-complete observations.*

### Correlation p-values: Predictors × Predictors

```{r predictors-corr-pvalues}
# predictors_fdr_mat already computed in predictors-corr-matrix chunk above
predictors_fdr_mat |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(across(everything(), \(x) {
    sig  <- !is.na(x) & x < 0.05
    xlab <- if_else(is.na(x), "—", as.character(round(x, 4)))
    cell_spec(xlab, bold = sig, color = if_else(sig, "#2166ac", "black"))
  })) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        caption = "P-values FDR-corrected across all 15 predictor pairs (bold = p (FDR) < .05).") |>
  apa_table()
```

# Aim 2 (Exploratory): Puberty and Raw Biomarker Levels

Correlations between pubertal development and raw biomarker levels at each timepoint (T1–T4).

```{r puberty-raw-levels, echo=FALSE}
biomarker_levels <- sos_crp_panel |>
  full_join(sos_cytokines_panel, by = c("SampleID", "Time")) |>
  full_join(sos_hormones_panel,  by = c("SampleID", "Time")) |>
  left_join(sos_puberty,         by = "SampleID") |>
  left_join(timing_df |> select(SampleID, age_menarche_c, PDS_F5), by = "SampleID")
```

```{r puberty-levels-corr, results='asis'}
# Pubertal status (PUBcomp) plus the two timing operationalizations that are
# used unadjusted elsewhere in this document (age at menarche, PDS F5
# perceived timing; see [Correlations: All Puberty Variables × Reactivity]).
# Status-for-age -- the third timing operationalization -- already has its
# own age-adjusted regression version just below ([Age-Adjusted Effect of
# Pubertal Status on Raw Biomarker Levels]), so it is not repeated here as a
# second, unadjusted correlation.
all_pub_label_map <- setNames(all_pub_labels, all_pub_vars)

for (pv in all_pub_vars) {
  cat("\n\n##", all_pub_label_map[[pv]], "\n\n")
  bio_vars <- c("CRP_log", "IL10_log", "IL6_log", "TNFalpha_log",
                "DHEA_log", "Testosterone_log", "Cortisol_log")

  corr_long <- map_dfr(bio_vars, function(bv) {
    map_dfr(1:4, function(tp) {
      dat <- biomarker_levels |>
        filter(Time == tp) |>
        select(all_of(c(bv, pv))) |>
        na.omit()
      if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
      ct <- cor.test(dat[[bv]], dat[[pv]])
      tibble(
        Biomarker = bv,
        Timepoint = paste0("T", tp),
        r         = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3),
        p_raw     = ct$p.value
      )
    })
  }) |>
    mutate(group = if_else(
      Biomarker %in% c("CRP_log", "IL10_log", "IL6_log", "TNFalpha_log"),
      "Immune", "Hormones"
    )) |>
    group_by(group) |>
    mutate(p_fdr = round(p.adjust(p_raw, method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
    ungroup()

  corr_tbl <- corr_long |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = Biomarker, names_from = Timepoint,
                values_from = c(r, p_fdr),
                names_glue = "{Timepoint}_{.value}") |>
    select(Biomarker, T1_r, T1_p_fdr, T2_r, T2_p_fdr, T3_r, T3_p_fdr, T4_r, T4_p_fdr)

  corr_tbl |>
    mutate(across(ends_with("_p_fdr"), \(x) cell_spec(
      round(x, 4), bold = !is.na(x) & x < 0.05,
      color = if_else(!is.na(x) & x < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black")
    ))) |>
    kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE,
          col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)")),
          caption   = paste0("Correlations: ", all_pub_label_map[[pv]],
                             " ", intToUtf8(215), " biomarker levels (FDR-adjusted within immune/hormones, 16/12 tests pooling all 4 timepoints; bold = p (FDR) < .05)")) |>
    add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "T1" = 2, "T2" = 2, "T3" = 2, "T4" = 2)) |>
    apa_table(full_width = FALSE) |>
    as.character() |>
    cat()
}
```

## Age-Adjusted Effect of Pubertal Status on Raw Biomarker Levels

The correlations above are unadjusted (each puberty/timing variable considered alone). Here each log-transformed biomarker level, at each timepoint, is regressed jointly on pubertal status (PUBcomp) and age at session, isolating the status-beyond-age effect -- i.e., the status-for-age timing operationalization -- the same way the reactivity models above do. Age at menarche and PDS F5 perceived timing are not re-tested here, since they are used unadjusted throughout (see the correlations above).

```{r puberty-levels-regressions}
biomarker_levels <- biomarker_levels |> left_join(age_df, by = "SampleID")

bio_vars_log    <- c("CRP_log", "IL10_log", "IL6_log", "TNFalpha_log", "DHEA_log", "Testosterone_log", "Cortisol_log")
bio_labels_map  <- setNames(
  c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", paste0("TNF-", intToUtf8(945)), "DHEA", "Testosterone", "Cortisol"),
  bio_vars_log
)

levels_joint_tbl <- map_dfr(bio_vars_log, function(bv) {
  map_dfr(1:4, function(tp) {
    dat <- biomarker_levels |>
      filter(Time == tp) |>
      select(all_of(c(bv, "PUBcomp", "age_at_session"))) |>
      na.omit()
    if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
    fit <- lm(as.formula(paste(bv, "~ PUBcomp + age_at_session")), data = dat)
    broom::tidy(fit) |>
      filter(term == "PUBcomp") |>
      mutate(Biomarker = bio_labels_map[bv], Timepoint = paste0("T", tp), n = nrow(dat))
  })
}) |>
  mutate(group = if_else(Biomarker %in% c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", paste0("TNF-", intToUtf8(945))), "Immune", "Hormones")) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = round(p.adjust(p.value, method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(estimate = round(estimate, 3))

levels_joint_tbl |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Biomarker, names_from = Timepoint, values_from = c(estimate, p_fdr),
              names_glue = "{Timepoint}_{.value}") |>
  select(Biomarker, T1_estimate, T1_p_fdr, T2_estimate, T2_p_fdr, T3_estimate, T3_p_fdr, T4_estimate, T4_p_fdr) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p_fdr"), \(x) cell_spec(
    x, bold = !is.na(x) & x < 0.05, color = if_else(!is.na(x) & x < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black")
  ))) |>
  kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "b", "p (FDR)", "b", "p (FDR)", "b", "p (FDR)", "b", "p (FDR)")),
        caption = "Effect of pubertal status on log biomarker level, controlling for age (FDR within immune/hormones; bold = p (FDR) < .05)") |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "T1" = 2, "T2" = 2, "T3" = 2, "T4" = 2)) |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

### Trend Plot: Age-Adjusted Effect of Pubertal Status on Raw Biomarker Levels

Same partial-residual approach as the reactivity trend plot above -- both pubertal status and each biomarker level are residualized on age at session (separately per timepoint), then plotted against each other. Rows are biomarkers, columns are timepoints (T1–T4).

```{r puberty-levels-trend, fig.width=11, fig.height=12, fig.cap="Age-adjusted effect of pubertal status on raw biomarker levels: partial-residual plots by biomarker and timepoint"}
levels_sig <- levels_joint_tbl |>
  mutate(sig = ifelse(p_fdr < 0.05, "FDR-significant (p < .05)", "Not significant")) |>
  select(Biomarker, Timepoint, sig)

levels_partial <- map_dfr(bio_vars_log, function(bv) {
  map_dfr(1:4, function(tp) {
    dat <- biomarker_levels |>
      filter(Time == tp) |>
      select(all_of(c(bv, "PUBcomp", "age_at_session"))) |>
      na.omit()
    if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
    resid_y <- resid(lm(as.formula(paste(bv, "~ age_at_session")), data = dat))
    resid_x <- resid(lm(PUBcomp ~ age_at_session, data = dat))
    tibble(Biomarker = bio_labels_map[bv], Timepoint = paste0("T", tp), resid_status = resid_x, resid_level = resid_y)
  })
}) |>
  left_join(levels_sig, by = c("Biomarker", "Timepoint")) |>
  mutate(
    Biomarker = factor(Biomarker, levels = unname(bio_labels_map)),
    Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = paste0("T", 1:4))
  )

ggplot(levels_partial, aes(x = resid_status, y = resid_level)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2, color = "grey30") +
  geom_smooth(aes(color = sig, fill = sig), method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.15) +
  facet_grid(Biomarker ~ Timepoint, scales = "free") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("FDR-significant (p < .05)" = "#2a78d6", "Not significant" = "#b9b8b2"), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FDR-significant (p < .05)" = "#2a78d6", "Not significant" = "#b9b8b2"), drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Pubertal status (residualized on age)",
    y = "Log biomarker level (residualized on age)",
    color = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0), strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

# Aim 3a: Fear of Negative Evaluation (FNE) and Biomarker Correlations

*Aim 3 (manuscript, primary individual-difference construct): Pearson correlations between BFNES total score and (a) log-transformed biomarker concentrations at each of the four timepoints (T1–T4), FDR-corrected separately within immune markers and hormones, and (b) each of the 13 reactivity difference scores, FDR-corrected within each reactivity domain.*

Fear of negative evaluation (FNE) is the primary individual-difference construct examined in this manuscript, consistent with a social-evaluative-threat framing of the SOS task: appraisal of social-evaluative threat is theorized to shape both subjective and biological stress responses, and BFNES is examined first among the individual-difference measures for that reason.

Correlations between BFNES (Brief Fear of Negative Evaluation Scale; Leary, 1983) total score and biomarker levels at each timepoint and biomarker reactivity. Items 2, 6, 7, and 10 were reverse-scored; total scores range from 12–60 with higher scores reflecting greater fear of negative evaluation.

```{r bfnes-desc}
bfnes |>
  filter(!is.na(BFNES_total)) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    Mean = round(mean(BFNES_total), 2),
    SD   = round(sd(BFNES_total),   2),
    Min  = round(min(BFNES_total),  2),
    Max  = round(max(BFNES_total),  2)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "BFNES descriptives") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

## FNE (BFNES) × Raw Biomarker Levels

```{r bfnes-levels-corr}
bfnes_levels <- biomarker_levels |>
  left_join(bfnes, by = "SampleID")

bfnes_corr_long <- map_dfr(bio_vars, function(bv) {
  map_dfr(1:4, function(tp) {
    dat <- bfnes_levels |> filter(Time == tp) |>
      select(all_of(c(bv, "BFNES_total"))) |> na.omit()
    if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
    ct <- cor.test(dat[[bv]], dat$BFNES_total)
    tibble(Biomarker = bv, Timepoint = paste0("T", tp),
           r = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3), p_raw = ct$p.value)
  })
}) |>
  mutate(group = if_else(
    Biomarker %in% c("CRP_log", "IL10_log", "IL6_log", "TNFalpha_log"),
    "Immune", "Hormones"
  )) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = round(p.adjust(p_raw, method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
  ungroup()

bfnes_corr_tbl <- bfnes_corr_long |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Biomarker, names_from = Timepoint,
              values_from = c(r, p_fdr),
              names_glue = "{Timepoint}_{.value}") |>
  select(Biomarker, T1_r, T1_p_fdr, T2_r, T2_p_fdr, T3_r, T3_p_fdr, T4_r, T4_p_fdr)

bfnes_corr_tbl |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p_fdr"), \(x) cell_spec(
    round(x, 4), bold = !is.na(x) & x < 0.05,
    color = if_else(!is.na(x) & x < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black")
  ))) |>
  kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)")),
        caption   = paste0("Correlations: BFNES ", intToUtf8(215), " biomarker levels (FDR-adjusted; bold = p (FDR) < .05)")) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "T1" = 2, "T2" = 2, "T3" = 2, "T4" = 2)) |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r bfnes-levels-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
sig_bfnes_levels <- bfnes_corr_long |> filter(p_fdr < 0.05)
n_sig_bfnes_levels <- nrow(sig_bfnes_levels)
bfnes_levels_sig_text <- if (n_sig_bfnes_levels == 0) {
  "No significant associations were observed after FDR correction"
} else {
  paste(
    paste0(sig_bfnes_levels$Biomarker, " at ", sig_bfnes_levels$Timepoint,
           " (r = ", sig_bfnes_levels$r, ", p~FDR~ = ", sig_bfnes_levels$p_fdr, ")"),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}
```

**Results.** BFNES total score was correlated with log-transformed biomarker concentrations at each timepoint (T1–T4). FDR correction was applied separately within immune markers and hormones. `r if (n_sig_bfnes_levels == 0) "No significant associations survived FDR correction." else paste0(n_sig_bfnes_levels, " significant association", if (n_sig_bfnes_levels != 1) "s were" else " was", " observed: ", bfnes_levels_sig_text, ".")`

## FNE (BFNES) × Reactivity

```{r bfnes-reactivity-corr}
bfnes_reactivity <- all_difference |>
  left_join(bfnes, by = "SampleID") |>
  select(-SampleID)

# Pairwise-complete: each reactivity outcome is tested on its own available
# n (na.omit() on just that outcome + BFNES_total), matching the pairwise
# convention Aim 2's rcorr() already uses and the raw-level BFNES
# correlations above (bfnes-levels-corr) already use. Previously this ran a
# single na.omit() on the full 13-column frame first, so every outcome was
# tested on the same listwise-complete n (bounded by the HR subsample) even
# though most outcomes don't need HR data to be non-missing.
bfnes_react_corrs <- map_dfr(setNames(reactivity_vars, reactivity_labels), function(rv) {
  dat <- bfnes_reactivity |> select(all_of(c(rv, "BFNES_total"))) |> na.omit()
  ct <- cor.test(dat[[rv]], dat$BFNES_total)
  tibble(n = nrow(dat), r = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3), p_raw = ct$p.value)
}, .id = "Reactivity") |>
  mutate(domain = case_when(
    str_detect(Reactivity, "^ΔHR")                                        ~ "HR",
    Reactivity %in% c("ΔCRP", "ΔIL-10", "ΔIL-6", "ΔTNF-α")             ~ "Immune",
    Reactivity %in% c("ΔDHEA", "ΔTestosterone", "ΔCortisol")             ~ "Hormones",
    TRUE                                                                   ~ "Subjective"
  )) |>
  group_by(domain) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = round(p.adjust(p_raw, method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
  ungroup()

bfnes_react_corrs |>
  select(Reactivity, n, r, p_fdr) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
    color = if_else(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Reactivity outcome", "n", "r", "p (FDR)")),
        caption = "Correlations: BFNES × reactivity (pairwise-complete n per outcome; FDR-adjusted; bold = p (FDR) < .05)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r bfnes-reactivity-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
sig_bfnes_react <- bfnes_react_corrs |> filter(p_fdr < 0.05)
n_sig_bfnes_react <- nrow(sig_bfnes_react)
bfnes_react_sig_text <- if (n_sig_bfnes_react == 0) {
  "No significant associations were observed after FDR correction"
} else {
  paste(
    paste0(sig_bfnes_react$Reactivity, " (r = ", sig_bfnes_react$r,
           ", p~FDR~ = ", sig_bfnes_react$p_fdr, ")"),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}
```

**Results.** BFNES total score (fear of negative evaluation; range 12–60) was correlated with each of the 13 reactivity difference scores. FDR correction was applied within each reactivity domain (HR: 4 tests; immune: 4 tests; hormones: 3 tests; subjective: 2 tests). `r if (n_sig_bfnes_react == 0) "No significant associations survived FDR correction." else paste0(n_sig_bfnes_react, " significant association", if (n_sig_bfnes_react != 1) "s were" else " was", " observed: ", bfnes_react_sig_text, ".")`

# Aim 3b: Depressive Symptoms (CES-DC, Exploratory) and Biomarker Correlations

*Aim 3 (manuscript, exploratory individual-difference aim): Pearson correlations between CES-DC total score and (a) log-transformed biomarker concentrations at each of the four timepoints (T1–T4), FDR-corrected separately within immune markers and hormones, and (b) each of the 13 reactivity difference scores, FDR-corrected within each reactivity domain.*

Depressive symptoms (CES-DC) are examined here as an exploratory individual-difference aim, not as an organizing construct of the manuscript; associations reported in this section should be interpreted accordingly and are not treated as evidence that pubertal or FNE-related biomarker findings function as depression risk factors.

```{r dep-desc}
dep |>
  summarise(
    n    = sum(!is.na(CESD_total)),
    Mean = round(mean(CESD_total, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD   = round(sd(CESD_total,   na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Min  = round(min(CESD_total,  na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    Max  = round(max(CESD_total,  na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "CES-DC descriptives") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

## CES-DC (Depressive Symptoms) × Raw Biomarker Levels

```{r dep-levels-corr}
dep_levels <- biomarker_levels |>
  left_join(dep, by = "SampleID")

bio_vars <- c("CRP_log", "IL10_log", "IL6_log", "TNFalpha_log",
              "DHEA_log", "Testosterone_log", "Cortisol_log")

dep_corr_long <- map_dfr(bio_vars, function(bv) {
  map_dfr(1:4, function(tp) {
    dat <- dep_levels |> filter(Time == tp) |>
      select(all_of(c(bv, "CESD_total"))) |> na.omit()
    if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
    ct <- cor.test(dat[[bv]], dat$CESD_total)
    tibble(Biomarker = bv, Timepoint = paste0("T", tp),
           r = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3), p_raw = ct$p.value)
  })
}) |>
  mutate(group = if_else(
    Biomarker %in% c("CRP_log", "IL10_log", "IL6_log", "TNFalpha_log"),
    "Immune", "Hormones"
  )) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = round(p.adjust(p_raw, method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
  ungroup()

dep_corr_tbl <- dep_corr_long |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Biomarker, names_from = Timepoint,
              values_from = c(r, p_fdr),
              names_glue = "{Timepoint}_{.value}") |>
  select(Biomarker, T1_r, T1_p_fdr, T2_r, T2_p_fdr, T3_r, T3_p_fdr, T4_r, T4_p_fdr)

dep_corr_tbl |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p_fdr"), \(x) cell_spec(
    round(x, 4), bold = !is.na(x) & x < 0.05,
    color = if_else(!is.na(x) & x < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black")
  ))) |>
  kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)", "r", "p (FDR)")),
        caption   = paste0("Correlations: CES-DC ", intToUtf8(215), " biomarker levels (FDR-adjusted p-values; bold = p (FDR) < .05)")) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "T1" = 2, "T2" = 2, "T3" = 2, "T4" = 2)) |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r dep-levels-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
sig_dep_levels <- dep_corr_long |> filter(p_fdr < 0.05)
n_sig_dep_levels <- nrow(sig_dep_levels)
dep_levels_sig_text <- if (n_sig_dep_levels == 0) {
  "No significant associations were observed after FDR correction"
} else {
  paste(
    paste0(sig_dep_levels$Biomarker, " at ", sig_dep_levels$Timepoint,
           " (r = ", sig_dep_levels$r, ", p~FDR~ = ", sig_dep_levels$p_fdr, ")"),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}
```

**Results.** CES-DC total score was correlated with log-transformed biomarker concentrations at each of the four timepoints (T1–T4). FDR correction was applied separately within immune markers (CRP, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-α) and hormones (DHEA, Testosterone, Cortisol). `r if (n_sig_dep_levels == 0) "No significant associations survived FDR correction." else paste0(n_sig_dep_levels, " significant association", if (n_sig_dep_levels != 1) "s were" else " was", " observed: ", dep_levels_sig_text, ".")`

## CES-DC (Depressive Symptoms) × Reactivity

```{r dep-reactivity-corr}
dep_reactivity <- all_difference |>
  left_join(dep, by = "SampleID") |>
  select(-SampleID)

# Pairwise-complete: see the identical note in the BFNES × Reactivity chunk
# above (bfnes-reactivity-corr) -- same fix, same rationale.
dep_react_corrs <- map_dfr(setNames(reactivity_vars, reactivity_labels), function(rv) {
  dat <- dep_reactivity |> select(all_of(c(rv, "CESD_total"))) |> na.omit()
  ct <- cor.test(dat[[rv]], dat$CESD_total)
  tibble(n = nrow(dat), r = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3), p_raw = ct$p.value)
}, .id = "Reactivity") |>
  mutate(domain = case_when(
    str_detect(Reactivity, "^ΔHR")                                        ~ "HR",
    Reactivity %in% c("ΔCRP", "ΔIL-10", "ΔIL-6", "ΔTNF-α")             ~ "Immune",
    Reactivity %in% c("ΔDHEA", "ΔTestosterone", "ΔCortisol")             ~ "Hormones",
    TRUE                                                                   ~ "Subjective"
  )) |>
  group_by(domain) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = round(p.adjust(p_raw, method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
  ungroup()

dep_react_corrs |>
  select(Reactivity, n, r, p_fdr) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
    color = if_else(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Reactivity outcome", "n", "r", "p (FDR)")),
        caption = "Correlations: CES-DC × reactivity (pairwise-complete n per outcome; FDR-adjusted; bold = p (FDR) < .05)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r dep-reactivity-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
sig_dep_react <- dep_react_corrs |> filter(p_fdr < 0.05)
n_sig_dep_react <- nrow(sig_dep_react)
dep_react_sig_text <- if (n_sig_dep_react == 0) {
  "No significant associations were observed after FDR correction"
} else {
  paste(
    paste0(sig_dep_react$Reactivity, " (r = ", sig_dep_react$r,
           ", p~FDR~ = ", sig_dep_react$p_fdr, ")"),
    collapse = "; "
  )
}
```

**Results.** CES-DC total score was correlated with each of the 13 reactivity difference scores. FDR correction was applied within each reactivity domain (HR: 4 tests; immune: 4 tests; hormones: 3 tests; subjective: 2 tests). `r if (n_sig_dep_react == 0) "No significant associations survived FDR correction." else paste0(n_sig_dep_react, " significant association", if (n_sig_dep_react != 1) "s were" else " was", " observed: ", dep_react_sig_text, ".")`

This check has moved to `sos-bioreactivity-supplement.qmd`, Section S3 (AUCi-Based Reactivity), which reports the full peak-vs-AUCi head-to-head table for CES-DC × all 13 reactivity outcomes. CES-DC is treated as an exploratory aim throughout.

# Sample Timing

## Inter-Sample Intervals

Time elapsed (minutes) from the T1 sample to each subsequent collection.

```{r timing-intervals}
saliva_timing |>
  select(elapsed_T2, elapsed_T3, elapsed_T4) |>
  summarise(across(
    everything(),
    list(
      n    = \(x) sum(!is.na(x)),
      Mean = \(x) round(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      SD   = \(x) round(sd(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      Min  = \(x) round(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      Max  = \(x) round(max(x, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
  )) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to  = c("Sample", ".value"),
               names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)") |>
  mutate(Sample = case_match(Sample,
    "elapsed_T2" ~ "T1 → T2",
    "elapsed_T3" ~ "T1 → T3",
    "elapsed_T4" ~ "T1 → T4"
  )) |>
  kable(caption = "Minutes elapsed from T1 to each subsequent sample") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

## Elapsed Time as Covariate in Hormone Models

Correlations between inter-sample elapsed time and hormone levels, to assess whether timing variation affects results.

```{r timing-hormone-corr, results='asis'}
hormone_timing <- sos_hormones_panel |>
  left_join(saliva_timing, by = "SampleID") |>
  mutate(elapsed = case_when(
    Time == 2 ~ elapsed_T2,
    Time == 3 ~ elapsed_T3,
    Time == 4 ~ elapsed_T4,
    .default  = NA_real_
  ))

hormone_vars <- c("DHEA_log", "Testosterone_log", "Cortisol_log")

cat("### Correlation: elapsed time × hormone level at T2–T4\n\n")
map_dfr(hormone_vars, function(hv) {
  map_dfr(2:4, function(tp) {
    dat <- hormone_timing |> filter(Time == tp) |>
      select(all_of(hv), elapsed) |> na.omit()
    if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
    ct <- cor.test(dat[[hv]], dat$elapsed)
    tibble(Hormone = hv, Timepoint = paste0("T", tp),
           r = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3), p = round(ct$p.value, 3))
  })
}) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Timepoint, values_from = c(r, p),
              names_glue = "{Timepoint}_{.value}") |>
  select(Hormone, T2_r, T2_p, T3_r, T3_p, T4_r, T4_p) |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), \(x) cell_spec(
    round(x, 3), bold = x < 0.05,
    color = if_else(x < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black")
  ))) |>
  kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Hormone", "r", "p", "r", "p", "r", "p")),
        caption = paste0("Elapsed minutes from T1 ", intToUtf8(215), " hormone level")) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "T2" = 2, "T3" = 2, "T4" = 2)) |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE) |>
  print()
```

## Time Since Waking × Sex Steroid Hormones

Wake time was recorded as free text; times after 12:00 pm were treated as implausible and set to missing. Elapsed hours = time of T1 collection minus wake time.

```{r wake-desc}
wake_time |>
  filter(!is.na(hours_since_wake)) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    Mean = round(mean(hours_since_wake), 1),
    SD   = round(sd(hours_since_wake), 1),
    Min  = round(min(hours_since_wake), 1),
    Max  = round(max(hours_since_wake), 1)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Hours elapsed from waking to T1 sample collection") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r wake-hormone-corr}
wake_hormones <- sos_hormones_panel |>
  filter(Time == 1) |>
  left_join(wake_time |> select(SampleID, hours_since_wake), by = "SampleID") |>
  left_join(
    hormones_difference |> select(SampleID, dhea_difference, test_difference, cort_difference),
    by = "SampleID"
  )

hormone_wake_outcomes <- c(
  "DHEA_log"        = "DHEA (T1 level)",
  "Testosterone_log" = "Testosterone (T1 level)",
  "Cortisol_log"    = "Cortisol (T1 level)",
  "dhea_difference" = "ΔDHEA (reactivity)",
  "test_difference" = "ΔTestosterone (reactivity)",
  "cort_difference" = "ΔCortisol (reactivity)"
)

map_dfr(names(hormone_wake_outcomes), function(hv) {
  dat <- wake_hormones |> select(all_of(hv), hours_since_wake) |> na.omit()
  if (nrow(dat) < 5) return(NULL)
  ct <- cor.test(dat[[hv]], dat$hours_since_wake)
  tibble(
    Outcome = hormone_wake_outcomes[[hv]],
    n       = nrow(dat),
    r       = round(unname(ct$estimate), 3),
    p       = round(ct$p.value, 3)
  )
}) |>
  mutate(p = cell_spec(p, bold = p < 0.05,
    color = if_else(p < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Outcome", "n", "r", "p")),
        caption = "Correlations: hours since waking × sex steroid hormone levels and reactivity") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

# Correlation Matrices by Domain

Circle size and color reflect correlation magnitude (red = negative, blue = positive). \* marks correlations significant at p < .05 (uncorrected).

```{r corr-raw-biomarker-alltp}
raw_alltp_rc <- rcorr(raw_alltp_mat)

# Long-format lookup of r / p / n for any pair of labels in the full matrix,
# used by panels A-C below.
alltp_marker_names <- c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", "TNF-α", "DHEA", "Testosterone", "Cortisol")
alltp_pair <- function(a, b) {
  tibble(
    r = raw_alltp_rc$r[cbind(a, b)],
    p = raw_alltp_rc$P[cbind(a, b)],
    n = raw_alltp_rc$n[cbind(a, b)]
  )
}
# Cell text: r to 2 decimals without the leading zero, * if p < .05
alltp_cell_label <- function(r, p) {
  lab <- sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf("%.2f", r))
  lab <- sub("^-(\\.00)$", "\\1", lab)  # no "-.00"
  if_else(is.na(r), "", paste0(lab, if_else(!is.na(p) & p < 0.05, "*", "")))
}
alltp_fill <- scale_fill_gradient2(
  low = "#d73027", mid = "white", high = "#4575b4",
  midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), breaks = seq(-1, 1, 0.5),
  name = "r", na.value = "grey95"
)
alltp_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.key.height = unit(1.6, "lines"))
```

### A. Stability of Each Biomarker Across Timepoints

stability_df <- map_dfr(alltp_marker_names, \(m) map_dfr(tp_pairs, \(tp) {

  b <- paste0(m, " (T", tp[2], ")")
  alltp_pair(a, b) |>
    mutate(marker = m, pair = paste0("T", tp[1], "–T", tp[2]))
})) |>

ggplot(stability_df, aes(pair, marker, fill = r)) +

# FDR Correction Audit

This section verifies that (1) FDR correction is applied using the correct family definitions throughout, and (2) significance markers in correlation matrices match the FDR-adjusted p-value tables.

## FDR Family Definitions

```{r fdr-audit-families}
tibble::tribble(
  ~Analysis,                         ~`FDR family`,                              ~`N tests`,
  "Biomarker time trends (LMM)",     "Immune markers (CRP, IL-10, IL-6, TNF-α)", "4",
  "Biomarker time trends (LMM)",     "Hormones (DHEA, Testosterone, Cortisol)",  "3",
  "Peak vs. T1 t-tests",             "Immune markers",                           "4",
  "Peak vs. T1 t-tests",             "Hormones",                                 "3",
  "Puberty × reactivity (corr)",     "HR outcomes (per puberty/timing var)",     "4",
  "Puberty × reactivity (corr)",     "Immune outcomes (per puberty/timing var)", "4",
  "Puberty × reactivity (corr)",     "Hormone outcomes (per puberty/timing var)","3",
  "Puberty × reactivity (corr)",     "Subjective outcomes (per puberty/timing var)","2",
  "Puberty × reactivity (regression)","Per predictor term across 13 outcomes",    "13",
  "Timing joint regression",          "Per predictor term across 13 outcomes",    "13",
  "CES-DC × biomarker levels",        "Immune markers (4 bio × 4 tp)",            "16",
  "CES-DC × biomarker levels",        "Hormones (3 bio × 4 tp)",                  "12",
  "CES-DC × reactivity",              "HR",                                       "4",
  "CES-DC × reactivity",              "Immune",                                   "4",
  "CES-DC × reactivity",              "Hormones",                                 "3",
  "CES-DC × reactivity",              "Subjective",                               "2",
  "BFNES × biomarker levels",         "Immune markers (4 bio × 4 tp)",            "16",
  "BFNES × biomarker levels",         "Hormones (3 bio × 4 tp)",                  "12",
  "BFNES × reactivity",               "HR",                                       "4",
  "BFNES × reactivity",               "Immune",                                   "4",
  "BFNES × reactivity",               "Hormones",                                 "3",
  "BFNES × reactivity",               "Subjective",                               "2"
) |>
  kable(caption = "FDR correction family definitions across all analyses") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

*Note: the exploratory end-of-document correlation matrices (Bioreactivity Measures, Outcome Measures, All Measures, and their raw-variable counterparts — Raw HR & Biomarker (T1) Measures, Raw Biomarker Levels (All Timepoints) HR & Subjective Stress, Raw Outcome Measures, Raw Puberty & Demographic Measures, All Raw Measures) display raw uncorrected p-values — they are descriptive only and not used for inference.*

## Raw vs. FDR Significant: Summary

```{r fdr-audit-summary}
# ── Puberty × reactivity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_pub_raw <- sum(raw_allpub_mat < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_pub_fdr <- sum(fdr_allpub_mat < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── Depression × levels ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_dep_lev_raw <- sum(dep_corr_long$p_raw < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_dep_lev_fdr <- sum(dep_corr_long$p_fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── Depression × reactivity ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_dep_rx_raw  <- sum(dep_react_corrs$p_raw  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_dep_rx_fdr  <- sum(dep_react_corrs$p_fdr  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── BFNES × levels ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_bf_lev_raw  <- sum(bfnes_corr_long$p_raw  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_bf_lev_fdr  <- sum(bfnes_corr_long$p_fdr  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# ── BFNES × reactivity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_bf_rx_raw   <- sum(bfnes_react_corrs$p_raw  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_bf_rx_fdr   <- sum(bfnes_react_corrs$p_fdr  < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

tibble::tribble(
  ~Analysis,                    ~`Total tests`, ~`Sig (raw p < .05)`, ~`Sig (FDR p < .05)`, ~`Lost to FDR`,
  "Puberty × reactivity",       nrow(raw_allpub_mat) * ncol(raw_allpub_mat), n_pub_raw, n_pub_fdr, n_pub_raw - n_pub_fdr,
  "CES-DC × biomarker levels",  nrow(dep_corr_long),   n_dep_lev_raw, n_dep_lev_fdr, n_dep_lev_raw - n_dep_lev_fdr,
  "CES-DC × reactivity",        nrow(dep_react_corrs), n_dep_rx_raw,  n_dep_rx_fdr,  n_dep_rx_raw  - n_dep_rx_fdr,
  "BFNES × biomarker levels",   nrow(bfnes_corr_long), n_bf_lev_raw,  n_bf_lev_fdr,  n_bf_lev_raw  - n_bf_lev_fdr,
  "BFNES × reactivity",         nrow(bfnes_react_corrs),n_bf_rx_raw,  n_bf_rx_fdr,   n_bf_rx_raw   - n_bf_rx_fdr
) |>

```

## Matrix vs. Table Agreement: Puberty

```{r fdr-audit-puberty-agree}
# The corrplot uses fdr_allpub_mat; the table also uses fdr_allpub_mat.
# These are the same object, so agreement is guaranteed — this chunk confirms it.
corrplot_sig <- fdr_allpub_mat < 0.05
table_sig    <- fdr_allpub_mat < 0.05

n_disagree <- sum(corrplot_sig != table_sig, na.rm = TRUE)

if (n_disagree == 0) {
  cat("✅ PASS: corrplot significance markers and FDR p-value table agree on all",
      sum(!is.na(fdr_allpub_mat)), "cells.\n")
} else {
  cat("❌ FAIL:", n_disagree, "cell(s) disagree between the corrplot and the table.\n")
  which(corrplot_sig != table_sig, arr.ind = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(row_label = all_pub_labels[row], col_label = reactivity_labels[col]) |>
    select(row_label, col_label) |>
    print()
}
```

## Matrix vs. Table Agreement: Depression & BFNES

```{r fdr-audit-dep-bfnes-agree}
# Dep and BFNES analyses have no corrplot — only the FDR tables.
# Check that p_fdr values in the stored objects match a fresh recomputation.

check_fdr <- function(long_df, group_var = "group", raw_col = "p_raw", fdr_col = "p_fdr", label = "") {
  recomputed <- long_df |>
    group_by(.data[[group_var]]) |>
    mutate(p_fdr_check = round(p.adjust(.data[[raw_col]], method = "fdr"), 4)) |>
    ungroup()

  n_mismatch <- sum(
    abs(recomputed[[fdr_col]] - recomputed$p_fdr_check) > 1e-6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  if (n_mismatch == 0) {
    cat("✅ PASS", label, "— stored p_fdr matches recomputed FDR on all rows.\n")
  } else {
    cat("❌ FAIL", label, "—", n_mismatch, "row(s) differ.\n")
  }
}

check_fdr(dep_corr_long,   label = "CES-DC × biomarker levels")
check_fdr(bfnes_corr_long, label = "BFNES × biomarker levels")

# Reactivity tables use domain grouping
check_fdr(dep_react_corrs,   group_var = "domain", label = "CES-DC × reactivity")
check_fdr(bfnes_react_corrs, group_var = "domain", label = "BFNES × reactivity")
```

```{r fdr-audit-puberty-detail}
# Show every cell where raw and FDR significance differ (informational only)
raw_sig_pub <- raw_allpub_mat < 0.05
fdr_sig_pub <- fdr_allpub_mat < 0.05

changed <- which(raw_sig_pub != fdr_sig_pub, arr.ind = TRUE)

if (nrow(changed) == 0) {

} else {

    `FDR sig`        = fdr_sig_pub[changed],
    check.names = FALSE
  ) |>
    arrange(`p (FDR)`) |>
    kable(caption = "Cells where raw p < .05 but FDR p ≥ .05 (or vice versa)") |>
    apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
}
```

# Supplementary: Responder vs. Non-responder Analyses

*This section is exploratory and supplementary — it was not part of the three pre-registered hypotheses. Dichotomizing a continuous reactivity measure into "responder"/"non-responder" throws away information and loses statistical power relative to treating reactivity as continuous (as the main analyses do). The "any post-baseline increase" threshold used below is also lenient: a single noisy sample above baseline is enough to be classified a responder, so measurement noise alone can inflate the responder group. Finally, the four steps below (responder definition, trajectory plots, the primary CES-DC test, and the exploratory extension) are not multiplicity-controlled against each other — only the 7 biomarker tests within each step are FDR-corrected. Treat this section as hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory.*

## Responder Definition & Counts

For each biomarker, participants are classified using a lenient "any post-baseline increase" rule: **Responder** = at least one of T2, T3, or T4 exceeds T1 (`max(T2, T3, T4) > T1`); **Non-responder** = no post-baseline sample exceeds T1. Participants need at least one non-missing post-T1 sample to be classified; otherwise they are excluded as insufficient data.

This differs from the peak-based reactivity measure used in the main analysis (Aim 1c continued) in two ways: it also considers T2 (the primary analysis only compares T1 to the larger of T3/T4), and it only requires *any single* post-baseline sample to exceed baseline rather than requiring the *larger of two* samples to exceed baseline. As a result, this responder definition is more lenient and is expected to classify more participants as "responders" than would show significant peak reactivity by the primary criterion.

```{r resp-define, echo=FALSE}
classify_responder <- function(data, value_col) {
  data |>
    select(SampleID, Time, value = all_of(value_col)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Time, values_from = value, names_prefix = "T", values_fn = mean) |>
    rowwise() |>
    mutate(
      post_max = suppressWarnings(max(c_across(any_of(c("T2", "T3", "T4"))), na.rm = TRUE)),
      post_max = if_else(is.infinite(post_max), NA_real_, post_max),
      responder_status = case_when(
        is.na(T1) | is.na(post_max) ~ NA_character_,
        post_max > T1                ~ "Responder",
        TRUE                          ~ "Non-responder"
      )
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(SampleID, responder_status)
}

responder_specs <- list(
  "CRP"          = list(data = sos_crp_panel,       col = "CRP_log"),
  "IL-10"        = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "IL10_log"),
  "IL-6"         = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "IL6_log"),
  "TNF-alpha"    = list(data = sos_cytokines_panel, col = "TNFalpha_log"),
  "DHEA"         = list(data = sos_hormones_panel,  col = "DHEA_log"),
  "Testosterone" = list(data = sos_hormones_panel,  col = "Testosterone_log"),
  "Cortisol"     = list(data = sos_hormones_panel,  col = "Cortisol_log")
)

biomarker_levels <- c("CRP", "IL-10", "IL-6", "TNF-α", "DHEA", "Testosterone", "Cortisol")

responder_df <- imap_dfr(responder_specs, function(spec, nm) {
  classify_responder(spec$data, spec$col) |> mutate(biomarker = nm)
}) |>
  mutate(
    biomarker = recode(biomarker, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α"),
    biomarker = factor(biomarker, levels = biomarker_levels)
  )

responder_summary <- responder_df |>
  group_by(biomarker) |>
  summarise(
    n_responder    = sum(responder_status == "Responder", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_nonresponder = sum(responder_status == "Non-responder", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_excluded     = sum(is.na(responder_status)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_classified  = n_responder + n_nonresponder,
    pct_responder = round(100 * n_responder / n_classified, 1)
  )

print(responder_summary, n = 20)

responder_summary |>
  select(biomarker, n_responder, pct_responder, n_nonresponder, n_excluded) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "n Responders", "% Responders", "n Non-responders", "n Excluded")),
        caption = "Responder classification counts by biomarker (any post-baseline sample > T1)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r resp-vs-peak, echo=FALSE}
peak_positive <- bind_rows(
  sos_crp_wide       |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "CRP",          peak_reactive = crp_peak  > CRP_log_1),
  sos_cytokines_wide |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "IL-10",        peak_reactive = il10_peak > IL10_log_1),
  sos_cytokines_wide |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "IL-6",         peak_reactive = il6_peak  > IL6_log_1),
  sos_cytokines_wide |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "TNF-α",   peak_reactive = tnfa_peak > TNFalpha_log_1),
  sos_hormones_wide  |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "DHEA",         peak_reactive = dhea_peak > DHEA_log_1),
  sos_hormones_wide  |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "Testosterone", peak_reactive = test_peak > Testosterone_log_1),
  sos_hormones_wide  |> transmute(SampleID, biomarker = "Cortisol",     peak_reactive = cort_peak > Cortisol_log_1)
) |>
  mutate(biomarker = factor(biomarker, levels = biomarker_levels))

resp_vs_peak <- responder_df |>
  filter(!is.na(responder_status)) |>
  inner_join(peak_positive, by = c("SampleID", "biomarker")) |>
  filter(!is.na(peak_reactive)) |>
  group_by(biomarker) |>
  summarise(
    n                       = n(),
    n_responder             = sum(responder_status == "Responder"),
    n_responder_also_peak   = sum(responder_status == "Responder" & peak_reactive),
    pct_responder_also_peak = round(100 * n_responder_also_peak / n_responder, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(resp_vs_peak, n = 20)

resp_vs_peak |>
  kable(escape = FALSE, col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "n (both defined)", "n Responders (any-increase)",
                       "...also peak-reactive (T3/T4 > T1)", "% overlap")),
        caption = "How the lenient any-increase responder definition compares to the peak-based (T3/T4 max) reactivity criterion") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r resp-counts-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
resp_pct_range <- paste0(min(responder_summary$pct_responder), "%–", max(responder_summary$pct_responder), "%")
resp_overlap_range <- paste0(min(resp_vs_peak$pct_responder_also_peak), "%–", max(resp_vs_peak$pct_responder_also_peak), "%")
```

**Results.** The proportion classified as responders under this lenient "any post-baseline increase" rule ranged from `r resp_pct_range` across the 7 biomarkers. Only `r resp_overlap_range` of responders (by this definition) also met the stricter peak-based reactivity criterion (T3/T4 max exceeding T1) used in the main analysis, confirming that the two definitions capture meaningfully different — and only partially overlapping — groups; the any-increase rule is substantially more permissive.

## Trajectory Plots

Each panel shows the mean (± SE) log-transformed trajectory across T1–T4 for responders vs. non-responders, with faint individual-participant lines in the background.

```{r resp-trajectory-data, echo=FALSE}
traj_data <- imap_dfr(responder_specs, function(spec, nm) {
  rs <- classify_responder(spec$data, spec$col)
  spec$data |>
    select(SampleID, Time, value = all_of(spec$col)) |>
    filter(!is.na(value)) |>
    left_join(rs, by = "SampleID") |>
    filter(!is.na(responder_status)) |>
    mutate(biomarker = nm)
}) |>
  mutate(
    biomarker = recode(biomarker, "TNF-alpha" = "TNF-α"),
    biomarker = factor(biomarker, levels = biomarker_levels)
  )

traj_summary <- traj_data |>
  group_by(biomarker, Time, responder_status) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value), se_val = sd(value) / sqrt(n()), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r resp-trajectory-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
ggplot(traj_data, aes(x = Time, y = value, group = SampleID, color = responder_status)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.12) +
  geom_line(data = traj_summary,
            aes(x = Time, y = mean_val, group = responder_status, color = responder_status),
            linewidth = 1.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(data = traj_summary,
                aes(x = Time, y = mean_val, ymin = mean_val - se_val, ymax = mean_val + se_val,
                    group = responder_status, color = responder_status),
                width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.6, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = traj_summary,
             aes(x = Time, y = mean_val, group = responder_status, color = responder_status),
             size = 1.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4, labels = paste0("T", 1:4)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = NULL, option = "C", begin = 0.2, end = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~biomarker, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Concentration (log-transformed)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

**Results.** By construction, responder trajectories rise above T1 at some point post-baseline while non-responder trajectories stay flat or decline; the value of this figure is in showing *where* that separation occurs (e.g., whether it appears already at T2, or only at T3/T4) and how much within-group spread (faint lines) surrounds each group mean. -->

<!-- ## Depressive Symptoms (Primary Supplementary Test)

For each biomarker, we tested whether CES-DC total score differs between responders and non-responders (Welch two-sample t-test; Wilcoxon rank-sum reported alongside as a robustness check given the likely skew of self-report symptom totals). Cohen's *d* uses the pooled-SD convention with the standard large-sample normal-approximation 95% CI; FDR correction is applied to the Welch-test p-values across the 7 biomarkers.

```{r resp-group-test-fn, echo=FALSE}
run_group_test <- function(rs_df, outcome_df, outcome_col) {
  d <- rs_df |>
    filter(!is.na(responder_status)) |>
    inner_join(outcome_df, by = "SampleID") |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome_col]]))

  resp    <- d[[outcome_col]][d$responder_status == "Responder"]
  nonresp <- d[[outcome_col]][d$responder_status == "Non-responder"]

  if (length(resp) < 2 || length(nonresp) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      n_responder = length(resp), n_nonresponder = length(nonresp),
      mean_responder = NA_real_, sd_responder = NA_real_,
      mean_nonresponder = NA_real_, sd_nonresponder = NA_real_,
      t_stat = NA_real_, df = NA_real_, p_welch = NA_real_,
      W_stat = NA_real_, p_wilcox = NA_real_,
      cohen_d = NA_real_, d_lower = NA_real_, d_upper = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  tt <- t.test(resp, nonresp)  # Welch by default (unequal variances)
  wt <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(resp, nonresp))

  n1 <- length(resp); n2 <- length(nonresp)
  pooled_sd <- sqrt(((n1 - 1) * var(resp) + (n2 - 1) * var(nonresp)) / (n1 + n2 - 2))
  d_val <- (mean(resp) - mean(nonresp)) / pooled_sd
  se_d  <- sqrt((n1 + n2) / (n1 * n2) + d_val^2 / (2 * (n1 + n2 - 2)))

  tibble(
    n_responder = n1, n_nonresponder = n2,
    mean_responder = mean(resp), sd_responder = sd(resp),
    mean_nonresponder = mean(nonresp), sd_nonresponder = sd(nonresp),
    t_stat = unname(tt$statistic), df = unname(tt$parameter), p_welch = tt$p.value,
    W_stat = unname(wt$statistic), p_wilcox = wt$p.value,
    cohen_d = d_val, d_lower = d_val - 1.96 * se_d, d_upper = d_val + 1.96 * se_d
  )
}

responder_by_biomarker <- split(responder_df, responder_df$biomarker)
```

```{r resp-cesdc-test, echo=FALSE}
cesdc_results <- imap_dfr(responder_by_biomarker, function(rs_df, nm) {
  run_group_test(rs_df, dep, "CESD_total") |> mutate(biomarker = nm, .before = 1)
}) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = p.adjust(p_welch, method = "fdr"))

print(cesdc_results, n = 20)

cesdc_results |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  select(biomarker, n_responder, n_nonresponder, mean_responder, sd_responder,
         mean_nonresponder, sd_nonresponder, t_stat, df, p_welch, p_wilcox,
         cohen_d, d_lower, d_upper, p_fdr) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
    color = if_else(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Biomarker", "n Resp", "n Non-resp", "M Resp", "SD Resp", "M Non-resp", "SD Non-resp",
                       "t (Welch)", "df", "p (Welch)", "p (Wilcoxon)", "Cohen's d", "d 95% LL", "d 95% UL", "p (FDR)")),
        caption = "CES-DC total score by responder status, per biomarker (FDR within the 7 biomarkers)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r resp-cesdc-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
cesdc_plot_data <- imap_dfr(responder_by_biomarker, function(rs_df, nm) {
  rs_df |>
    filter(!is.na(responder_status)) |>
    inner_join(dep, by = "SampleID") |>
    filter(!is.na(CESD_total)) |>
    mutate(biomarker = nm)
}) |>
  mutate(biomarker = factor(biomarker, levels = biomarker_levels))

ggplot(cesdc_plot_data, aes(x = responder_status, y = CESD_total, fill = responder_status)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.4, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.08, size = 1, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "C", begin = 0.2, end = 0.85, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~biomarker, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "CES-DC total score") +

```

```{r resp-cesdc-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
cesdc_sig <- cesdc_results |> filter(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05)
n_cesdc_sig <- nrow(cesdc_sig)
cesdc_sig_text <- if (n_cesdc_sig == 0) "" else
  paste(cesdc_sig$biomarker, collapse = ", ")
```

**Results.** `r if (n_cesdc_sig == 0) "No biomarker showed a significant CES-DC difference between responders and non-responders after FDR correction across the 7 biomarkers." else paste0(n_cesdc_sig, " of 7 biomarkers showed a significant CES-DC difference between responders and non-responders after FDR correction: ", cesdc_sig_text, ".")` Given the caveats above — lost power from dichotomizing a continuous measure, and a lenient threshold that likely includes some noise-driven "responders" — these results should be treated as preliminary signals for follow-up with continuous reactivity models, not as confirmatory evidence of a responder/depression link.

## Exploratory: Other Group Differences

*Clearly exploratory.* The same responder/non-responder groups are compared here on BFNES (fear of negative evaluation), pubertal status (PUBcomp composite), age at session, and BMI — none of which were pre-specified for this comparison. FDR correction is applied separately within each outcome, across the 7 biomarkers (4 independent FDR families).

```{r resp-exploratory-test, echo=FALSE}
exploratory_outcomes <- list(
  "BFNES total"     = list(data = bfnes,      col = "BFNES_total"),
  "Pubertal status" = list(data = sos_puberty, col = "PUBcomp"),
  "Age at session"  = list(data = age_df,      col = "age_at_session"),
  "BMI"             = list(data = bmi,         col = "BMI")
)

exploratory_results <- imap_dfr(exploratory_outcomes, function(spec, outcome_name) {
  imap_dfr(responder_by_biomarker, function(rs_df, nm) {
    run_group_test(rs_df, spec$data, spec$col) |> mutate(biomarker = nm, .before = 1)
  }) |>
    mutate(outcome = outcome_name, .before = 1)
}) |>
  group_by(outcome) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = p.adjust(p_welch, method = "fdr")) |>
  ungroup()

print(exploratory_results, n = 40)

exploratory_results |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  select(outcome, biomarker, n_responder, n_nonresponder, mean_responder, sd_responder,
         mean_nonresponder, sd_nonresponder, t_stat, df, p_welch, p_wilcox, cohen_d, p_fdr) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = cell_spec(p_fdr, bold = !is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05,
    color = if_else(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05, "#2166ac", "black"))) |>
  kable(escape = FALSE,
        col.names = italicize_stats(c("Outcome", "Biomarker", "n Resp", "n Non-resp", "M Resp", "SD Resp",
                       "M Non-resp", "SD Non-resp", "t (Welch)", "df", "p (Welch)", "p (Wilcoxon)",
                       "Cohen's d", "p (FDR)")),
        caption = "Exploratory group comparisons: BFNES, pubertal status, age, and BMI by responder status (FDR within each outcome, across the 7 biomarkers)") |>
  apa_table(full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r resp-exploratory-results-vals, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
explor_sig <- exploratory_results |> filter(!is.na(p_fdr) & p_fdr < 0.05)
n_explor_sig <- nrow(explor_sig)
explor_sig_text <- if (n_explor_sig == 0) "" else
  paste0(explor_sig$outcome, " (", explor_sig$biomarker, ")", collapse = "; ")
```

**Results.** `r if (n_explor_sig == 0) "None of the exploratory group comparisons (BFNES, pubertal status, age at session, BMI) reached significance after FDR correction within each outcome across the 7 biomarkers." else paste0(n_explor_sig, " exploratory comparison(s) reached significance after FDR correction: ", explor_sig_text, ".")` As noted above, this extension was not pre-specified and is reported for hypothesis-generation only; it is not corrected for the additional comparisons across the four outcome variables or against the CES-DC test above. -->
